#2602. Tommy DeVito embracing latest chance to be NFL starting QB

"Tommy Cutlets" has been in this spot before.

Former Giants quarterback Tommy DeVito, who became a household name in New York, is getting another chance to be in the pressure cooker as a starting signal caller.

This time his task is to replace the injured Drake Maye, who suffered a fractured right fibula in the Patriots' blowout loss to the Lions in Germany on Nov. 15.

Maye is expected to be out at least six weeks, and though head coach Mike Vrabel hopes Maye can return at some point of the season, it's no guarantee he will be ready to return for New England in 2026.

Tommy DeVito, who is replacing injured starter Drake Maye, is all smiles as he talks to reporters during a news conference before the Patriots' practice on Nov. 24, 2026, in Foxborough, Mass. AP

Either way, the chances of the Patriots (5-5), who are coming off a bye, to make the playoffs will hinge on how well DeVito plays, and that starts Sunday with a road test against the 1-9 Chargers, who suffered a loss to the Jets this past week.

"Everybody has embraced me from the first snap and first play I had last week (in the loss to Detroit)," DeVito told reporters, referring to an outing in which he struggled, completing just 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison. "I've put my best foot forward in trying to earn their trust."

During the 2023 season with the Giants, DeVito, a northern New Jersey native, showed he can provide a spark when he was forced into the lineup after Daniel Jones and Tyrod Taylor suffered injuries.

In that six-game span, "Tommy Cutlets" led Big Blue to three straight victories in which he became the first undrafted free agent rookie since 1970 to have three consecutive games with a passer rating higher than 100. But he couldn't sustain the strong play and was benched again by Brian Daboll for a once-again healthy Taylor during a loss to the Eagles later in the season.

DeVito, who is 3-5 as a starter, started two games for Big Blue in the 2024 season after the Giants benched and waived Jones, but an arm injury and concussion sent him to the sidelines as Drew Lock started the final six games.

He became the odd man out after the Giants signed veterans Russell Wilson and Jameis Winston and following the selection of Jaxson Dart in the first round of the 2025 draft.

The Giants cut DeVito that summer but hoped to re-sign him to the practice squad after he cleared waivers. Instead, he was claimed by the Patriots.

DeVito spent the 2025 season on the practice squad behind Maye and Josh Dobbs but then supplanted Dobbs as Maye's backup when Dobbs was released. He signed a two-year extension worth up to $7.4 million with $2 million guaranteed.

Tommy DeVito throws a pass during the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Germany. Kirby Lee-Imagn Images

Vrabel knows the intangible spark DeVito can bring to a team, but says the time he had working with the Patriots' wide receivers during training camp will benefit him, as well as the starters' reps he has received this week.

"A lot of energy. I think a lot of work in there with those guys," Vrabel said. "I think he's taken advantage of his opportunities. I think he's also improved, just fundamentally. … Those things probably didn't show up with the exposure from his last game and when he got into it. But I think being able to see some of these things, work on them, focus on them and understand what it is that he can do a little bit better, I think that that'll obviously help him and in turn, help us.″

DeVito — who said offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels and quarterbacks coach Ashton Grant "want me to be me" — is pumped up for his latest chance to lead a team as a starter.

"You feel more energized for sure. It's time to go. Injuries are part of the game, unfortunately. For the players that are in that position, that's how you get opportunities," DeVito said.

49ers quarterback Brock Purdy dropping back to pass in an NFL game against the Vikings. Getty Images

#2594. Aaron Rodgers benched vs. Broncos; Steelers will start Mason Rudolph at QB instead

The Pittsburgh Steelers announced Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers will be inactive.

NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported after the announcement that the decision was head coach Mike McCarthy's. There are no reports that Rodgers is dealing with an injury.

The Steelers didn't offer any explanation beyond a statement from team spokesman Burt Lauten announcing the roster move:

"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos.

"Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game on Friday."

Rodgers, a future Hall of Famer, may have played his last NFL game. He announced before the season started that this would be his last in the league. It's a stunning development for the 6-4 Steelers and a quarterback who is one of the best to ever play the game.

Aaron Rodgers is no longer the starting quarterback for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Rodgers, 42, is in his 22nd NFL season and well beyond his prime. He's in his second season with the Steelers, who hired McCarthy in the offseason in part because of his previous relationship with Rodgers.

McCarthy coached Rodgers for 13 seasons during Rodgers' prime and the pair won a Super Bowl together in Green Bay. Rodgers won two his four NFL MVP's while playing for McCarthy.

But with a playoff berth in the balance, McCarthy and the Steelers have decided 10 games into their season that Rudolph gives them a better chance at making the postseason.

Tuesday's news drops one day after McCarthy gave Rodgers what appeared to be clear vote of confidence.

"Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," McCarthy told reporters in his Monday news conference.

That statement came on the heels of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. The loss was the second straight for Pittsburgh and snapped a seven-game losing streak for an Eagles team that's been in a tailspin for most of the season.

Even with the consecutive losses, the Steelers remain on the right side of the playoff picture. If the postseason started this week, Pittsburgh would play as the final wild-card team and the No. 7 seed in the AFC.

Rodgers had displayed continued signs of decline this year with statistically his worst career season. But there are worse starting quarterbacks in the NFL. And it's questionable whether Rudolph, an established NFL backup, gives the Steelers a better chance at winning.

In 10 starts, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his passes for 6.2 yards per attempt and 224.1 yards per game with 16 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. The Steelers rank 23rd in total offense, 22nd in passing offense and 22nd in scoring offense with 21.4 points per game.

Rudolph is a seven-year NFL veteran in his sixth season with a Steelers team that selected him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft.

In 38 career appearances, Rudolph has completed 64.2% of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt with 30 touchdown and 22 interceptions. He's made 19 career starts, but has never established himself as an NFL starter.

With their postseason hopes on the line against a stout Broncos defense, the Steelers are ready to give Rudolph another chance in favor of their aging future Hall of Famer.

#2591. NBA Cup 2026: Celtics avert disaster, Mavs roll listless Nuggets, Pistons deny Magic without Cade Cunningham

The Boston Celtics entered halftime of Tuesday's NBA Cup game apparently well on their way to snapping a four-game losing streak.

They eventually got there. But it wasn't easy as they had to fend off a furious comeback effort from the Washington Wizards.

The Celtics opened an 80-49 lead at halftime that the Wizards cut to 117-112 in the final four minutes. But the Celtics held on from there to avert disaster via a 131-116 victory.

A Jayson Tatum 3 and two more by Baylor Scheierman in the game's final minutes helped ensure that the Celtics got back into the win column.

With the win, the Celtics improved to 3-0 in NBA Cup play to maintain control of East Group C. The Wizards dropped to 2-2 in the NBA Cup.

Tatum led the effort with 41 points, 8 assists and 6 rebounds. He shot 6 of 15 from 3, but made all of them before halftime as cold second-half 3-point shooting helped the Wizards mount their rally.

The Celtics were red-hot in the first half while shooting 15 of 26 (57.7%) from long distance. They shot 7 of 25 (28%) after halftime and needed three of those in the final minutes after the Wizards cut their deficit to five points.

Ultimately, their 43.1% success rate from 3 was a cornerstone of their win, but questions will surely surface about the wisdom of continuing to hoist up 3s after building a 31-point lead.

Paul George had no such struggles with a 28-point, 9-assist effort in which he shot 6 of 9 from 3. Anthony Davis led the Wizards with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 2 blocks and 1 steal.

Cooper Flagg was the best player on the floor Tuesday night in a Mavericks win over the Nuggets.

In a matchup of a former NBA champion and four-time MVP against a lineup featuring a rising NBA start, youth prevailed in Denver.

Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks rolled a listless Nuggets team in Denver to the tune of a a 120-101 win.

The Mavericks limited the Nuggets to 17 first-quarter points, then closed the second quarter with a 15-0 run to take a 58-39 lead into the break.

The Nuggets answered with a 38-point third quarter and cut it as close as 80-77. But the Mavericks answered the run and closed the game strong to silence Ball Arena down the stretch with an overwhelming win.

Flagg led seven Mavericks players in double figures with 24 points, a career-high 12 assists and 6 rebounds.

Jamal Murray countered with 20 points and 3 rebounds on a 6-of-17 shooting effort. Nikola Jokić had a relatively quiet scoring night with 18 points, 11 rebounds, 5 assists and 5 turnovers.

With the win, the Mavericks (10-7) improved to 3-0 in Cup play to take control of West Group A. The Nuggets (10-5) dropped to 2-1 in the NBA Cup to fall behind the Mavs.

Cade Cunningham was a late scratch and watched Tuesday's Pistons win in street clothes.

The Detroit Pistons secured an NBA Cup win over the Orlando Magic, but it was overshadowed by concern for Cade Cunningham, who was a late scratch due to a lingering knee injury.

The Pistons played without their All-NBA guard and cruised to a 104-86 win to hand the Magic their first loss in NBA Cup play. The Pistons (11-6) are now 2-1 in Cup play, while the Magic (7-10) drop to 3-1. The loss blocked the Magic from from a chance to clinch East Group A.

Cunningham was listed as probable prior to the game due to lingering knee soreness. But he was a late scratch before an NBA Cup game, raising concern that his injury is one that could further linger.

Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff declined to offer details on Cunningham's condition in his pregame news conference. He also didn't say much to tamp down concern.

"He's battling through a lot, and I'll leave it at that," Bickerstaff said. "He's going to go out and compete and give us what he's got. But he's fighting through a lot."

Cunningham had previously missed one game this season, last Wednesday's 122-109 win over the New Orleans Pelicans. He struggled in his previous outing with a season-low five points in Sunday's 107-97 loss to the Atlanta Hawks.

Detroit struggled to get its offense going early without Cunningham as the Magic jumped out to a 22-16 first-quarter lead on their home court. But the Pistons seized control with a 32-14 advantage in the second quarter and kept the Magic at bay from there.

Isaiah Joe took Cunningham's place in the starting lineup and finished the game with a team-high 21 points alongside 4 rebounds and 1 steal. Daniss Jenkins was the primary playmaker in Cunningham's absence with 15 points and 10 assists. Desmond Bane led the Magic with 21 points and 5 assists.

George is in the midst of a career renaissance in his first season with the Celtics.

Wizards guard Kyshawn George learned the hard way Tuesday night. With the Celtics up big in the second half, Paul sized up Kyshawn in isolation.

He gained some separation with an arm extension on the perimeter, then crossed Kyshawn over as he drove to his right. Kyshawn did not stay with him.

Instead, Kyshawn fell on his backside onto the court and into the legs of his teammate, Anthony Davis.

Paul picked up his dribble and waited a beat while shooting a glance at Kyshawn — just to make sure Kyshawn was watching. Only then did Paul pull up for a jumper from just inside the 3-point arc that sank through the net to extend Boston's lead to 90-65 en route to its 15-point win.

Week 12 of the NFL season kicks off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense. The Pittsburgh Steelers announced Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

The Niners releasing Aiyuk marked the end of a months-long standoff between the team and player. Payton did not get into specifics and told reporters he would not comment further on the situation.

Dobbins, 27, is in his second season with the Broncos. He has rushed for 324 yards and 3 touchdowns on 99 carries, adding 31 receiving yards on 9 catches. Last year, Dobbins compiled 772 rushing yards and 4 TDs.

The suspension leaves Denver will be without its leading rusher for Friday's Week 12 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jonah Coleman (302 rushing yards in 6 games) will presumably take over as the starter.

Micah Parsons is officially activated off the Physically Unable to Perform list, Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst announced on Tuesday.

So the All-Pro pass rusher appears to be ready to play in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams. Parsons had been listed as questionable for the game.

Running back Josh Jacobs is also "questionable" for the Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium.

He's been recovering from surgery on the ring finger he fractured.

Taking over after Drake Maye was injured in Week 10's game versus the Detroit Lions, DeVito completed 12-of-24 passes for 81 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Vrabel said he was impressed by the backup QB's performance and the improvement he's shown since training camp, even if the Patriots didn't win the game.

The plan is for Sam Darnold to start against the 49ers on Sunday, but Mike Macdonald wants to see the quarterback in practice first before making a final decision.

Darnold has been out for two games due to a quad injury suffered in Week 8.

Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem.

They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics said they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East.

Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start. They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams. It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants.

"We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play."

Yet, they knew what was being said about them.

Manchester United have had the most difficult start to a season in memory.

One of their biggest issues has been in attack as first-choice striker Benjamin Šeško has spent most of the season on the sidelines with injury.

Danish striker Rasmus Hojlund signed for the club from Atalanta in 2023 but was sold after just two seasons at the club.

Hojlund impressed on loan last season at SSC Napoli and the Italians made his move permanent in the summer.

The striker had his fair share of critics when he was at the club, scoring just 26 times in 95 appearances for the Red Devils.

The 23-year-old did remind English fans of his potential yesterday, though, when he scored Napoli's opener against Manchester City in their 2-2 draw in the Champions League.

After scoring the opening goal of the match, he mouthed to the crowd, "there's only one club in Manchester – Manchester United."

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match (via The Express), he doubled down on his comments during the match.

He explained, "Indeed (that's what I said). Some good banter, you know. There's the rivalry between City and United and I have a past with United. That's my club. Nothing against Man City, but United is a big club. It was good to score here."

Hojlund has made no secret of being a supporter of the club, and he stated when he left in the summer, "to say goodbye to Manchester United is something that kinda feels emotional too. My childhood dream came true by playing at Old Trafford in a red jersey."

#2586. The Bellingham effect, Vinicius’ lifeline | Three takeaways from PSV 1-5 Real Madrid

A disastrous first-half performance from Real Madrid and an early penalty for PSV handed the visitors the lead at the Santiago Bernabeu last night.

They held the lead heading into the half-time break, but what followed after they returned to the field was nothing less than a hurricane.

Real Madrid came back after the break more motivated than ever and began suffocating PSV in their own area with brilliant attacking football. A great goal from Federico Valverde then handed them an equaliser.

Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. then joined the party and added four goals to the scoreline, completing PSV's demolition and registering a massive scoreline.

Madrid Universal brings you three takeaways from Real Madrid 5-1 PSV Eindhoven.

Jose Mourinho's starting XI against PSV Eindhoven saw the manager make some big changes, and understandably so, given how crucial rotations are.

Jude Bellingham scored a sensational goal vs PSV. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Dean Huijsen, Ibrahima Konate and Jude Bellingham all started on the bench, and all three came on later in the game to reprieve the team.

Of them, Bellingham's cameo was the one that well and truly turned the game around, and in some style.

With the Englishman on the bench, Real Madrid struggled to dominate the game or create chances of their own. They created an xG of just 0.24 compared to PSV's 1.50, and conceded four big chances.

Throughout the first half, Los Blancos looked unmotivated, sluggish and slow to react to PSV's attacks, but everything changed after Bellingham came on.

The Englishman instantly brought purpose, energy and directness to Real Madrid's play, catalysing the team's performance and bringing the best version out of his teammates.

In 45 minutes, he racked up three key passes, earned one assist and scored one goal against PSV while also completing 95% of his passes. His presence on the field brought verticality to Real Madrid's buildup, and he alone provided eight carries and completed one dribble.

It is no surprise that the second-half xG for Real Madrid went up to a staggering 4.53 – a clear indication of how ruthless the team became with the Englishman on the field.

As promised, Jose Mourinho handed Vinicius Jr. a start against PSV in the UEFA Champions League last night, and the player was under serious pressure to perform as he was staring at a real risk of losing his starting spot in the team.

Vinicius Jr. finally found the net for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

His performance last night may not have been vintage, but it surely was a big step up from where he has been all season.

Vinicius played all 90 minutes at the Santiago Bernabeu, and he finally looked like a genuine goalscoring threat. He was lively down the left flank, and while he may not have shown his dribbling best, he did show glimpses of his vintage self.

In 90 minutes, the winger took four shots and scored one goal for Real Madrid. He hit the woodwork twice and missed two chances.

Further, the player looked connected to the buildup as he completed 83% of his passes and even earned one key pass. Vinicius completed one successful dribble and made a staggering ten progressive carries.

There is indeed still a long way to go before Vinicius returns to his Ballon d'Or campaign level, but Real Madrid and Mourinho will be encouraged by what they saw last night. Between his great international break and decent start to club football after the hiatus, there is reason to believe the old Vinicius could return.

The win over the Dutch opposition last night was Real Madrid's fifth in as many UEFA Champions League games this season, and takes them right to the top of the table, and PSG remain the only other side that can catch up in terms of points.

Real Madrid are unbeaten in the Champions League. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Just five matchdays into the campaign, Los Blancos already have fifteen points to their name and are now within touching distance of a top-8 finish.

Over the past two seasons, Real Madrid have consistently missed out on the top-8 by narrow margins, and have been forced to play an additional round in the competition in both seasons.

Historically, 16 points have been enough to secure a top-8 finish, and with Real Madrid already having fifteen with three games to go, it is safe to say they have all but qualified.

Just one point in their next three games will be enough to secure a top-8 finish, and while Arsenal may be a tricky opposition, they have games against LASK and Shakhtar remaining.

The target for Jose Mourinho and Co., needless to say, will be to finish as high as possible on the standings and thereby earn the second-leg home advantage all the way through the knockouts. Given their current position, even a top-1 finish is completely possible.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2583. Barcelona first-team regular a major doubt for Champions League clash vs Sabah due to knee discomfort

Joan Garcia is doubtful to play Barcelona's Champions League meeting with Sabah in Baku on Wednesday, November 25, after renewed discomfort in his right knee.

According to a recent report from Mundo Deportivo, the 24-year-old goalkeeper is still dealing with bone oedema and finished Sunday's La Liga match against Villarreal in pain.

Barcelona have not confirmed an official injury, but the situation has prompted the club to assess whether Garcia should feature in Azerbaijan or receive additional rest.

Garcia's discomfort is particularly concerning because it affects the same right knee that forced him to stop playing in September. Although his recovery had been progressing positively, the problem has not completely disappeared.

As such, the goalkeeper trained on Monday and remained under observation as Barcelona evaluated his response to the latest discomfort. Fortunately, his symptoms improved with rest, making a cautious approach a realistic option.

Joan Garcia is doubtful for the UCL clash against Sabah. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The club's medical staff, Flick and Garcia himself, will jointly determine whether he is fit enough to play against Sabah, as the decision will depend on his physical condition and the potential benefits of allowing him more time to recover.

It must be noted that Barcelona have a capable alternative in Dominik Livakovic if the coaching staff decide against risking their first-choice goalkeeper.

The Croatian international was seen warming up intensely during the Villarreal match, suggesting that Barcelona were prepared for the possibility of Garcia needing to come off.

However, the Spaniard tested his condition and elected to continue until the final whistle.

That decision allowed Garcia to complete the match, but it also increased the need to manage his workload more carefully while the knee discomfort persists.

Joan Gacria's knee discomfort has returned. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images)

Barcelona previously confirmed in September that Garcia was experiencing mild discomfort in his right knee, with his return dependent on his recovery.

The latest problem therefore requires careful monitoring rather than being treated as an entirely unrelated issue.

For what it is worth, the Sabah fixture comes during a busy period for Barcelona, with several important domestic and European matches approaching before Christmas.

Giving Garcia a rest in Baku could provide valuable recovery time and reduce the possibility of aggravating a problem that has already interrupted his season, while also allowing Livakovic to take responsibility in a Champions League match.

Understandably, Barcelona will want to ensure Garcia returns to full fitness and does not force himself into unnecessary strain just for the sake of playing.

#2582. Pistons vs Magic final score: Detroit’s dominant defense shows up with Cade Cunningham sidelined

The Goin to Work Pistons showed up tonight. Detroit dispatched the Orlando Magic 104-86. This was another statement game. It doesn't matter who plays; defense travels. Detroit is now 2-1 in NBA Cup play with a plus-31 point differential. Orlando felt Detroit's defensive wrath, holding Orlando to 14 second-quarter points. They were everywhere.

Cade Cunningham was a late scratch, but the next man steps up here. Both teams struggled to put the ball in the hoop, but Detroit generated better shots. They swung the ball from side to side on plenty of possessions. The shot-making results weren't always there, but their process was solid. It was probably more than solid considering they were down three starters tonight.

Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins picked up more on-ball reps. Jenkins had a 15-point and 10-assist double-double. Thompson continues to grow as a playmaker for others as he added seven more assists tonight.

Ausar seems much more sure of himself this season. Even the moments he turns down shots to find a teammate are telling — everything seems planned.

Ausar wasn't the only Piston with an all-around A performance. Kevin Huerter finished with 13-5-6. He worked the off-ball screen here, slightly froze the big, and threw an accurate lob to Paul Reed.

Isaiah Joe led the team with 21 points. He went 5-for-11 from trey. Joe showed off the range and confidence. He pressured the ball on the other end. Shooters competing on defense, and not being must-hide defenders, is such a plus. Joe is picking it up.

Ron Holland has success from deep. He buried two 3s. Detroit shot it well as a team despite their low point total. They went 15-for-36 from deep compared to Orlando's 12-for-36. John Collins, Woo, and Elijah Harkless (he made some momentum-swinging ones) all hit two 3s.

Detroit knocked down 3s but kept Orlando from doing anything. Franz Wagner had been on a hot streak until he ran into this defense (29 PPG over the last 10). He (20 pts) and Desmond Bane (21 pts) put numbers on the board, but it wasn't easy. Those two saw a crowd every time they drove the ball. Wagner started spamming push shots that felt automatic, but Detroit held him in check.

Anthony Black was a non-factor offensively tonight. That's a testament to Detroit's D, as he's been rolling all year. The Magic missed so many shots at the rim. They were initially dominating Detroit on the offensive glass, but those missed shots eventually turned into Detroit run-outs.

The Pistons also got their hands on so many Magic passes tonight. They made Orlando creators play with multiple hands in their faces and trusted their closeouts to disrupt "open" Orlando 3s. Holding a team under 90 in 2026 is some Goin to Work stuff. Hats off to J.B. Bickerstaff for having this defense ready to go at all times.

Detroit's final group play cup game is Friday versus the flaming hot Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks. Detroit could still win the group even after losing to the Toronto Raptors last Friday. They might need some help, but must start by handling their business with the Bucks.

#2581. Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers in stunning move in QB's final season

In a stunning development late Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Pittsburgh Steelers announced that quarterback Mason Rudolph would start in Week 12's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos. Team PR spokesman Burt Lauten gave no reason for the change but only revealed that Aaron Rodgers, the team's QB1 since the start of the 2025 season, would be inactive for a matchup with significant playoff ramifications for both teams.

However, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the pivot from Rodgers to Rudolph is a performance-based one that was made by head coach Mike McCarthy and effectively a benching of the 42-year-old four-time league MVP.

In Pittsburgh's most recent game, a 19-16 defeat to the largely decimated Philadelphia Eagles, who had lost seven games in a row entering last Sunday's contest, Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes but only for 227 yards and a TD. Rodgers' 6.2 yards per pass attempt is the lowest of his 22-year career since he became a full-time starter in 2008 and discounting his 2023 campaign with the New York Jets, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles tear on the first drive of opening night.

The first-year coach and native Pittsburgher spoke to reporters hours before the team's late-night announcement about Rodgers. McCarthy gave no indication he would bench a player he's been paired with most of his head coaching career, the duo spending nearly 13 seasons together with the Green Bay Packers.

"I just think the first thing comes to mind is wealth of knowledge and experience. I mean, there's really not a spot that he hasn't been in, so I think that's clearly evident. Our conversation this morning, probably half of it was going through different games over the years that reminds you of this, reminds you of that, the team we're getting ready to play," McCarthy said earlier Tuesday when asked about Rodgers.

"So, he just has a tremendous amount of experience and expertise, and I think that's a tool that his teammates and coaches are fortunate to have."

McCarthy did say as recently as Monday that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback" when asked about the possibility of mixing some of the other teams passers into the gameplan.

The coach also lamented the team's recent lack of offensive balance on Tuesday and the resulting impact on the pass game.

"We need to run the ball better, but we need to run it more," said McCarthy. "I mean, it's just like anything − a good run game starts with attempts. So, but we definitely got to run the ball, and then with that, the action pass game opportunities I feel will increase."

After a midseason surge in production from running back Jaylen Warren and the ground game, the Steelers have only managed 175 rushing yards total while dropping their past two games. And despite being in the top quartile of passes thrown league-wide, Pittsburgh has not gotten many explosive plays through the air nor sufficient production from wideouts like DK Metcalf.

The coach and quarterback have mostly had a very successful NFL collaboration over the course of their relationship, notably teaming to take the Packers to victory in Super Bowl 45, that storied franchise's most recent championship, to cap the 2010 season.

However the relationship had frayed to a degree by the time McCarthy was fired in Green Bay with four games left in the 2018 season. Rodgers has largely plastered over that period in subsequent years and typically speaks highly of McCarthy.

However the quarterback was caught on Prime Video's cameras in a Week 4 loss at Cleveland while screaming at McCarthy from the field and demanding a play call. The coach was subsequently caught muttering an expletive with a frustrated look on his face.

"I think it is a positive," Rodgers said in the aftermath while downplaying the incident. "Player-led teams are the best teams. I think anytime you're seeing the fire and the passion from all those guys, it's a good thing."

McCarthy has not addressed Rodgers' deactivation for the upcoming game, and Lauten's statement provided no insight into the decision. No NFL rule would preclude the Steelers from reversing course or asking Rodgers to back up Rudolph. But a decision as seismic as this one, combined with Rodgers' stature, would seem to make that highly unlikely. The Steelers also did not specify if Rodgers could return as the starter in Week 13, but that also seems improbable, barring further information.

Now in his second year with the Steelers, Rodgers had already indicated the 2026 season would be his final one. His one-year contract is set to pay him $22.5 million, fully guaranteed.

A ninth-year veteran, Rudolph was selected by the Steelers in the third round of the 2018 draft. He's spent all but one season of his NFL career in Pittsburgh, mostly serving as a backup to Rodgers, Ben Roethlisberger and Kenny Pickett. Rudolph has been one of the league's better Plan B QBs, going 8-5-1 in 14 regular-season starts for Pittsburgh.

Yet this also isn't the first time the Steelers have called him out of the bullpen late in the season. Rudolph replaced then-QB2 Mitch Trubisky late in the 2023 season when Pickett was injured. However then-coach Mike Tomlin kept Rudolph in the lineup, including Pittsburgh's playoff game at Buffalo, even when Pickett was healthy enough to play. Rudolph ended the regular season by winning all three of his starts and compiling a gaudy 118.0 passer rating. However, the overmatched Steelers were soundly beaten 31-17 by the Bills in the wild-card round, though Rudolph passed for 229 yards and two TDs.

#2578. The Shortlist: Real Sociedad gem Jon Martin is well worth €60m punt for Barcelona, Real Madrid and Premier League heavyweights

The talented centre-back has established himself as a key player at the Anoeta, breaking into Spain's senior squad in the process

Real Sociedad have gone to great lengths to secure the future of their most treasured asset over the last year. In October 2025, the Basque club extended Jon Martin's contract through to 2031, and nine months later, they felt compelled to improve his terms again as a host of European giants began circling for his signature.

The 20-year-old extended until 2032, with a reported €60 million (£50m/$66m) release clause added into the contract, and the club said in a glowing official statement: "Jon Martin is the present and the future of the club... a pillar of the Realista backline." That last part is certainly true, but Martin will be a target for the elite once again next year if he continues on his current trajectory, and €60m will be a small price to pay.

According to Sky Sports, "some of the biggest Premier League clubs" are keeping tabs on Martin, who made his senior debut for Spain in a June friendly clash with Iraq. Real Madrid and Barcelona are also being linked with the Sociedad star, but it could easily be argued that his qualities are an even better fit for the English top-flight than La Liga.

La Real have a proud history of producing world-class talent from their academy, with the likes of Antoine Griezmann and Xabi Alonso learning their trade at the Anoeta before becoming superstars elsewhere, and there is every chance that Martin could be their next big success story.

After six years earning his stripes in La Real's academy, Martin got his chance at first-team level in a crucial fixture

Martin was born in Lasarte-Oria near San Sebastian, and took inspiration from his father, Santiago, when taking his first steps into football. Santiago played for La Real between 1897 and 1992, before being forced to retire at just 21 after suffering a severe knee injury.

La Real spotted that the family talent had been passed on in 2018 as they drafted a 12-year-old Martin into their youth ranks. From there, he developed as both a defensive midfielder and centre-back, which shaped the composure he has on the ball these days, and took in a brief loan spell with SD Beasain in 2022.

In early 2023, Martin bypassed traditional age-group steps to make three appearances for Real Sociedad C, before advancing to the B squad ahead of the 2023-24 campaign. The teenager also became captain of Spain's Under-17 team, leading them out at both the U17 European Championship and U17 World Cup.

Sociedad B finished ninth in the Spanish third tier in Martin's sole year with the squad, and he anchored the defence with remarkable composure across 26 appearances, also chipping in with two goals. Martin's aerial dominance in both boxes was crucial to La Real securing a ninth-placed finish, and he earned his senior La Liga debut before the season ended.

Head coach Imanol Alguacil threw Martin on for Kieran Tierney for the final 23 minutes of a clash with Real Betis, and the 18-year-old settled into the backline without a hitch, helping La Real preserve a clean sheet in a 2-0 victory that sealed European qualification.

"I was really happy they thought of me for such an important match," Martin said when reflecting on that moment to Marca. "In a debut you always have that touch of nerves, but once you step onto the pitch, nothing - they disappear."

Despite the uncertainty caused by a revolving door of managers, Martin continued to go from strength to strength

Martin was integrated permanently into the first-team squad for the 2024-25 season, and made 17 appearances across all competitions as La Real reached the semi-finals of the Copa del Rey and last-16 of the Europa League. They did, however, only manage an 11th-placed finish in La Liga, and Alguacil decided to step down after six years in charge.

He was replaced by Sociedad B coach Sergio Francisco, who already had a strong bond with Martin, and though the youngster found himself behind Duje Caleta-Car in the early months of Franciso's reign and suffered a frustrating injury setback, the manager eventually made Martin the centrepiece of his defence upon his return in October.

Martin excelled in an initial four-match unbeaten run, earning widespread plaudits for his distribution and assured one-vs-one defending, but La Real then lost three matches in a row to sit just one point above the relegation zone by mid-December, and Francisco was relieved of his duties.

Losing such a close ally was a blow for Martin, but Francisco's successor, Pellegrino Matarazzo, also took an immediate liking to the Spanish centre-half. Matarazzo immediately lifted the squad's confidence levels, winning four and drawing three of his first seven league games, with a 2-1 home triumph over Barcelona the highlight as Martin led a gruelling low-block effort to frustrate the likes of Lamine Yamal and Fermin Lopez.

Most pundits put Barca's failure down to bad luck on the night, but Matarazzo was quick to point out how much work Martin and his team-mates put in, telling reporters: "Being alert is not luck. Throwing yourself in front of the ball is not luck - it's being aware of the moment."

Martin was one of La Real's standout players in their stunning Copa del Rey final triumph over Atletico Madrid

Matarazzo managed to drag his team back up to 10th in La Liga, which would have been enough to justify his appointment alone, but the American tactician also immortalised himself at the Anoeta by delivering the club's fourth Copa del Rey trophy. La Real edged out Osasuna on penalties in the round of 16, beat Alaves 3-2 in the quarter finals, and overcame bitter rivals Athletic Club in a Basque derby semi-final tie, winning both legs 1-0, to set up a blockbuster final meeting with Atletico Madrid.

After a 2-2 draw across normal and extra-time in Seville, La Real prevailed 4-3 in a tense penalty shootout. Martin produced a colossal display with nine duel wins, 13 clearances and 17 ball carries, also completing 92 percent of passes in his own half.

"Jon Martin is a fighter. He settled into the match. After the first 15 minutes, he played a fantastic game," Matarazzo said in his post-match press-conference. "He is a very important player for us because he brings a lot of emotion, a lot of fighting spirit. He can ignite the fans. I think he had a great game today."

It was no surprise that Luis de la Fuente drafted Martin into the Spain squad after that, and he was unlucky not to make the cut for the 2026 World Cup or the manager's first two squads of the current season. Dean Huijsen is in pole position to become Pau Cubarsi's long-term partner in the heart of the Roja defence, with Aymeric Laporte entering the latter stages of his career at 32, but De la Fuente won't be able to ignore Martin if he keeps progressing so rapidly.

To unlock the full scope of his talent, Martin would be best served by leaving his La Liga comfort zone

Indeed, Martin has been one of the best defenders in La Liga during the opening four months of the 2026-27 campaign. He ranks in the top five percent among all centre-backs in Europe's top five leagues for aerial duel and general duel win rate, and is now the first name on Matarazzo's teamsheet.

Sociedad have broken into La Liga's top five, four points clear of Sevilla in the race for what could prove to be a Champions League qualification spot, while they have also been billed as dark horses for the Europa League. With only five points from four games in the league phase, La Real have lacked a killer edge in Europe, but there were significant signs of improvement in a 1-1 draw against Lyon last time out.

Martin is already up to 15 starts in all competitions and his continued presence is essential as La Real strive to win more silverware and qualify for the Champions League. If they achieve either of those objectives, there's a good chance Martin will be in extremely high demand next summer.

In October, he told Sky Sports that "everything I need to be able to perform at a top level is here at this club", but also admitted he is grateful for the interest he's receiving, adding: "I think that I am a player people like." That should give his suitors a glimmer of hope.

Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool have all been named on that ever-growing list, with the latter perhaps the most attractive potential destination. As a press-resistant defender comfortable dribbling out of danger and breaking the lines with his passing, Martin would be ideally suited to fellow San Sebastian native Andoni Iraola's transition-heavy 4-2-3-1 system.

Martin is tailor-made for the higher tempo and more set-piece driven style of Premier League football, too, and would be a major weapon in both penalty areas. Of course, it would be a much easier transition if he were to pick Barca or Madrid, but it feels like he is already close to his ceiling in La Liga.

Liverpool would be wise to get ahead of the competition before Martin's value increases. Whatever happens, though, he's got an extremely bright future ahead of him.

The Boston Celtics traveled to Washington to face the Wizards in their third game of the NBA Cup Group C on Tuesday night. The Wizards started Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, and Alexandre Sarr. The 2026 NBA number 1 pick, AJ Dybantsa, hit the first points of the game with a two-point jumper. Boston hit their first 4 shots of the game as they got out to an early 9-2 lead. AJ Dybantsa scored the first 4 points for Washington against his favorite team growing up.

Neemias Queta had two early lob dunks and 8 early points for Boston against the double-big lineup of Washington. Tatum and George had one bucket each, but it was all Neemias Queta to start the game for the visitors.

Baylor Scheierman and Payton Pritchard were the first Celtics off the bench for Boston. Ron Harper Jr. also checked into the game for first-quarter minutes for Boston as the coaching staff seemingly searching for a spark after 3 straight road losses.

Chris Cenac Jr. checked into the game late in the quarter and provided some defensive hustle for Boston. Payton Pritchard nailed a deep logo triple for his first score of the game. Washington had just 34 points at the midway point of the second quarter. Tatum, George, and Queta had outscored the entire team, as the Celtics were in cruise control up by 23 points, 57-34.

Jayson Tatum returned to the game with a big lead, and he scored 8 straight points as Boston was dominating the Wiz. Tatum had 28 points and 5 assists in the first half, shooting 6 of 9 from downtown, as the team was primed for a third straight NBA Cup win.

This story is just getting started. Rodgers will surely have a reaction. And it surely won't be a shrug of the shoulders and an acceptance that he won't even be in uniform for the game.

#2566. Trevor Connelly enters Calder conversation in Golden Knights’ win over Edmonton

EDMONTON—It is almost shocking that Trevor Connelly is not discussed more often when discussing favorites for the Calder Trophy.

While there are certainly deserving candidates, Connelly has consistently stayed at or near the top among all rookies in goals and points. Even on a contending team like the Vegas Golden Knights have been year in and year out, Connelly has gone from the prospect Kelly McCrimmon refused to move to one of the most electrifying weapons the team has in their arsenal. Head coach Ryan Craig has already placed an immense amount of trust in Connelly since their days together in Henderson, and the rookie has done nothing but earn every bit of the praise he has received.

With the Golden Knights in the only game of the night on Tuesday, Connelly introduced himself on the national stage with a convincing effort in his first foray against the Edmonton Oilers, as the Golden Knights battled to a 5-3 victory at Rogers Place.

Early on, the Oilers looked the part of a team returning home from a six-game road trip.

A high sticking penalty from Oilers defenseman Mattias Ekholm would give the Golden Knights a double minor to work with, and the power play would ultimately take advantage. Jack Eichel would land a perfectly placed shot from the left faceoff dot to the far post, beating goaltender Devon Levi to break the ice.

Mitch Marner's primary assist would be the 600th of his career, while Victor Olofsson would continue his point-per-game pace on the secondary helper with his 13th point in as many games.

Marner would continue to make an impact in the first period, pressuring Shakir Mukhamadullin into a turnover directly to Connelly. The rookie would then skate unopposed to the front of the net and beat Levi with an impressive backhand shot to give the Golden Knights some breathing room.

The Oilers thought they had cut the lead back to one when Vasily Podkolzin's shot sneaked past the goal line, but it was determined that Mathieu Joseph knocked Carter Hart's stick out of his hand to trigger goaltender interference.

That play would ultimately wake the Oilers up from their first-period malaise. First, Evan Bouchard would unleash a rocket from the point that shattered Colton Dach's stick on its way past Hart. While the Vegas goaltender would keep his team in the lead, the dam would finally break after Jeremy Lauzon's broken stick would give Connor McDavid enough space to tie the game with seconds to go in the middle frame.

Even more concerning, however, was Hart being slow to get up after attempting to stop McDavid. Adin Hill would replace him to finish the period, but Hart would return to close out the game.

With both teams dominating one period, the Golden Knights would come out firing. Nic Dowd would begin with his first goal of the season with a close-range shot, followed by Eichel finishing an odd-man rush with Connelly to reclaim a two-goal lead.

Podkolzin would score seconds after Eichel to cut down the lead, but the Golden Knights remained resilient to hold things down until Connelly scored the empty net goal for his first three-point outing in the NHL.

The game pushed Connelly to 19 points on the year, overtaking Chicago Blackhawks forward Roman Kantserov for the lead among all rookies.

The Golden Knights will return to Nevada to celebrate Thanksgiving with their families, then take to the road once again for a Black Friday afternoon matinee against the San Jose Sharks.

#2564. Pittsburgh benching Aaron Rodgers

Pittsburgh Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Week 12 against the Denver Broncos, according to a team statement on Tuesday, Nov. 24. Mason Rudolph will draw the start in his place.

Why It Matters: Well, there's a bit to unpack here. First of all, the team waiting until after 11 PM ET on a Tuesday night to announce a quarterback change is highly unusual. The fact that it is happening to someone of Rodgers' ilk - regardless of the perception of how he is playing right now - is even more hard to believe. Then there is the dynamic of Rodgers' long-standing relationship with head coach Mike McCarthy. While no reason was given why the change was made in the statement, it seems obvious that Rodgers either did something that could be perceived as "conduct detrimental to the team" over the last 24-48 hours or McCarthy (or the front office) determined that his play has fallen off to the point that he is worthy of being benched. If it is the latter (which it likely is), it should not come as much of a surprise if Rodgers' release is coming shortly. Rudolph will make his 20th career start (in his seventh NFL season) and has typically performed reasonably well when called upon, but make no mistake about it: he is not a quality NFL starter. Rudolph's "promotion" will most likely benefit managers who use the Denver D/ST this week more than anyone else.

#2563. Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams announced the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He said at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

Hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a New Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a new era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an issue in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a big reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

In the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

In the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but New Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

If we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That said, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

With all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

The addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

If there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B

#2561. Kawhi Leonard is back on the (practice) court: will his return be enough?

The Raptors have released another brief statement outlining Kawhi Leonard's return to playing NBA basketball, and while there are positive signs emerging, little can be confirmed about when the forward will be back on the court.

"He has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address left knee swelling," stated the press release issued earlier today, November 24th. Leonard has not seen the court for more than one month, last having suited up in game two for the Raptors on October 23rd in a win for Toronto against the Washington Wizards.

Without Kawhi, the Raptors have been in free-fall, punctuated by a six-game losing streak earlier in November. Some of these were close, against good teams; the Raptors would develop a lead, then give it away in the second half, breaking the hearts of Toronto fans who tuned in to watch. With his clutch genes and scoring prowess, Leonard's presence on the team would have been sure to change the outcome of some of these games, but the lack of his presence has revealed both flaws, and upsides with this roster.

The Raptors roster, as currently constructed, is not that different from what it was last year. Regardless of having Leonard or Brandon Ingram at small-forward, these two players were signed for the same job: take offensive responsibilities off of Scottie Barnes' shoulders so that he can focus on playmaking and defence.

All together, a sound idea for roster construction. But the state of the starters around the pairs in both years? Less than ideal. The Raptors are currently ranked 24th in three-pointers made, and are shooting 33.8% from deep this season. A big reason for this is because this year, 3 of 5 Raptors starers are not considered good three point shooters, those being Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl, and RJ Barrett, while the two perceived marksmen, Immanuel Quickley, and Kawhi Leonard, have both been unreliable.

While the Raptors, ironically, have quite a few good three point shooting players or prospects coming off their bench, the Raps' starting lineup, the players who they have committed the most money to, are either non-shooters, in a shooting slump, or injured. While a lack of clutch play and poor defence is also certainly to blame for the Raptors' losses, being able to buy a 3 certainly would help the Raptors, especially in the fourth quarter of games.

It's not 2006 anymore, and the Raptors need to get with the times. Giving Ja'Kobe Walter more minutes is a step in the right direction, but with his certain relegation to the bench when Kawhi Leonard returns, the Raptors' rotations need to consistently sport players who can make long range shots.

As a whole, the Raptors have added Leonard to a problematic roster which in many respects, he was meant to, and seemed potentially able to fix. But, succeeding with Leonard always comes contingent with being able to survive the regular periods of absence he takes as a result of health issues. And the Raptors have shown themselves largely unable to do so.

One of the lone bright spots in the Raptors' season thus far has been the ascension of Scottie Barnes to hitherto unforeseen levels. Barnes has been thrust into a primary offensive creation role and has taken to it unexpectedly well. As of November 24th, Barnes is averaging almost 25 points per game and a career high in steals. He's doing it playing an antiquated style of basketball, too, barely making any threes, and living off of midrange buckets.

Barnes has never had a higher profile, nor has he ever been more fun to watch on the offensive side of the ball.

Allen Graves, the Santa Clara rookie drafted 19th overall, has done a lot to increase his volume from three, and had his first signature game, with a 20 point, 10 rebound performance to help the Raptors put away the Detroit Pistons. While it's unlikely for that same level of play to extend the rest of the season, Graves has shown that he's capable of doing what he was drafted to do, and could be the next developmental success story for the Raptors.

Getting Leonard back to pair with Barnes, Graves, and Collin Murray-Boyles gives the Raptors a disgusting forward rotation to lean on heavily, and Leonard's offensive abilities will likely be able to drag the Raptors back into a positive win/loss ratio. But, ideally, Leonard should not be dragging dead weight behind him. The Raptors, as an organization, need to take account of the state of their team without Kawhi Leonard. He won't always be available to bail out this roster, and when he isn't, it is irresponsible coaching and management to allow the roster to go on to lose games in the manner that they are currently losing them in.

Leonard is not being paid to help rookies ascend and find their place in the NBA. This is team headlined by professional, veteran players, and Leonard or no-Leonard, they should look like it on the basketball court.

The Raptors will give more information on Kawhi's health in a week. Stay frosty.

#2560. Aaron Rodgers couldn't play forever, and he might have an unceremonious end at age 42

Few players get the John Elway or Peyton Manning sendoff, winning a Super Bowl then announcing their retirement a few weeks or months later.

Still, it seemed like Aaron Rodgers would have a gentler ending to his great career than a short statement at 11:10 p.m. on a Tuesday.

The Pittsburgh Steelers made a stunning move, announcing that not only would Rodgers be replaced as the team's starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos, he wouldn't even be active for the game.

There were four MVPs, 10 Pro Bowls, a Super Bowl championship, dozens of highlights that defied belief over 22 seasons, and it all seems to end with a quick statement from the team after most of Pittsburgh had already gone to sleep.

It's not like Rodgers has played great this season, which he said will be his last in the NFL. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was asked this week if Rodgers was still the team's starter, so it wasn't completely out of the blue that he got benched.

It was abrupt, and with some unusual timing. There was no time to celebrate the end of a legendary career or even realize that the snaps he took Sunday might be his last.

It's just done, barring some other turn of events over the final few weeks of the season.

Aaron Rodgers looks around during the national anthem before last week's game, which was the 267th of his NFL career. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images)

Rodgers played OK this year. The Steelers couldn't have expected much more from a quarterback who will turn 43 on Dec. 2. No other quarterback, other than Tom Brady, had any reasonable level of success at Rodgers' age.

Rodgers threw for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns with six interceptions in 10 games. The Steelers won six of those games and if the season ended now, they'd be in the playoffs. Rodgers wasn't great, often throwing short as he did last season, which was reflected in him having the fourth-worst EPA (expected points added) among all qualified quarterbacks. It still didn't seem like he'd be benched.

It wasn't like the Steelers were giving the job to a hotshot rookie who will excite the fan base. Rudolph has been decent as a backup throughout his career, and he had a stretch in 2023 when the Steelers won all three of his starts that helped them to the playoffs. But the Steelers didn't feel any urgency to see what Rudolph can do. They just apparently felt Rodgers had already hit the age cliff and they saw it over the last two games.

After a solid start to the season there were two miserable performances from Rodgers and the team. He threw incomplete on his first seven passes in a blowout loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 10. That was the first time in his career he had started 0-for-7. Pittsburgh's loss on Sunday in Philadelphia was ugly, with the Steelers not scoring a touchdown until the final two minutes. Undrafted rookie Max Hurleman, making his NFL debut, might have become a trivia answer: He caught the Steelers' only touchdown against the Eagles, and it might end up being the final touchdown pass of Rodgers' career. As it stands, that could be the final play of Rodgers' career. Pittsburgh never got the ball back after that.

The Steelers were slumping. But the way the week unfolded makes the benching quite odd.

The Steelers have a short week. When asked Monday about Rodgers and possibly benching him, McCarthy gave a terse answer: "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." Then less than 48 hours later, with a game less than three days away, the Steelers made a change at quarterback.

The benching likely happened before 11 p.m. on a Tuesday but that's when the NFL world found out, making it one of the odder quarterback announcements in recent memory. And the decision to demote Rodgers all the way to at least No. 3 on the depth chart (the Steelers are the rare team that carries four quarterbacks) was made by a coach with whom Rodgers won a Super Bowl with at the end of the 2010 season. There wasn't anything pleasant about the move or how it was handled, and an NFL legend like Rodgers probably deserved better. But the league isn't much on sentiment, especially for teams on two-game losing streaks in a playoff race.

Maybe there will be more details to the benching, other than a coach who definitively said Monday that Rodgers was his quarterback completely changing his mind on a Tuesday (a day when the Steelers had a walkthrough practice), three days before his team plays the 8-2 Broncos.

Rodgers has spent most of his career, particularly the final few years of it, living in defiance. His confidence never wavered, whether talking about politics, criticizing the media or showing up teammates and even his coach on the field when he felt he wasn't at fault for a bad play. It never seemed he'd leave the game unless it was on his terms. Perhaps he gets a start later in the season if Rudolph doesn't play well or there are injuries or simply to give an all-time great a better sendoff than a social media blast late in the evening.

But there's a good chance we've suddenly seen the last of Rodgers on a football field, especially with the team making sure the world knew he wouldn't even be active Friday. The NFL can be a cold business, even for someone who was one of the faces of the league for a couple decades.

#2550. Maikel Garcia trade grades: Mariners land Gold Glove infielder; Royals get pitching help, but with huge risks

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Kansas City Royals and Seattle Mariners have struck the offseason's first blockbuster trade. The Mariners have acquired third baseman Maikel Garcia in a six-player trade, the teams announced on Wednesday. The Royals receive righties Logan Evans and Bryce Miller and lefty Jose A. Ferrer in the deal.

Garcia, 26, battled hand and hamstring injuries in 2026, but still managed a 1.8 WAR season in 88 games thanks to league-average offense and spectacular third base defense. He is a year removed from a 5.6 WAR season and receiving MVP votes. Garcia is signed long-term as well. He's owed a very reasonable $52.5 million through 2030, with a club option for 2031.

The 28-year-old Miller headlines the return for Kansas City. An oblique strain delayed the start to his 2026 season, but once healthy, he threw 118 ⅔ innings with a 4.17 ERA and under-the-hood numbers that were hit (3.70 expected ERA) or miss (4.41 FIP). Miller threw 180 ⅓ innings with a 2.94 ERA in 2024, and will remain under team control through 2029.

Ferrer, 26, is a workhorse ground ball reliever with three years of control remaining. McArthur (fracture) and Evans (Tommy John) both missed 2026 with elbow surgery. McArthur pitched in four minor-league rehab games in September and should be ready for spring training. Evans has surgery in January and is expected back at midseason.

Here now are our grades for this three-for-three swap between 2027 American League postseason hopefuls.

The Mariners came into the offseason with an opening at third base, a glaring need to improve their defense, and more starters than rotation spots. That all came to a head in this trade. They used Miller, their least effective starter the last two seasons, and two spare parts to net a long-term solution at the hot corner in Garcia, who plays Gold Glove-caliber defense.

One player alone won't fix Seattle's defense, of course, but Garcia is a very big step toward improving a unit that ranked 26th in defensive runs saved and 30th (by a lot) in outs above average. As for the lineup, new manager Jason Kanzler can run out something like this most days:

Donovan was limited to 39 games by two groin strains and a concussion this past season. He's very versatile and needn't be locked into DH. The Mariners can play Donovan in the outfield to open up DH at-bats for slugger Lazaro Montes, who hit some titanic home runs during his MLB debut in 2026. They could also move Donovan around to give others DH days.

The lineup and the defense are improved, and the Mariners still have a formidable rotation that includes Kade Anderson, Logan Gilbert, Emerson Hancock, George Kirby, and Bryan Woo. Right-hander Ryan Sloan, arguably the top pitching prospect in baseball (it's either Sloan or Anderson), is knocking on the door and figures to debut at some point in 2027.

Seattle will miss Ferrer in their bullpen but also have close to an entire offseason (minus a lockout) to replace him. Assuming the Mariners won't break the bank for Adrian Morejon, the free agent market still offers solid second- and third-tier lefty reliever options in A.J. Minter, Sean Newcomb, JoJo Romero, Gregory Soto, and Alex Vesia. Ferrer is a quality reliever but not irreplaceable.

Before his elbow fracture, which ultimately required three surgeries, McArthur showed a very lively curveball and strong ground ball ability. He's a middle reliever more than a high-leverage option, but is not merely a throw-in. Langevin struck out 106 batters in 55 ⅓ Single-A relief innings thanks to his mid-90s fastball in 2026. He also walked 39 batters, however.

Garcia received MVP votes a year ago thanks to a .286/.351/.449 line with 16 home runs and 23 stolen bases. He also runs some of the game's best contact rates. That's his upside and maybe 2025 was a career year, but Garcia has a reasonably high floor thanks to his defense. Getting even league-average offense moving forward makes this a win for Seattle.

The free agent market is flush with No. 3-4 type starters and light on position players, specifically non-first base infielders. Couldn't the Royals keep Garcia and just sign a pitcher or two? There is something to be said for Miller's cost control as an arbitration-eligible player, of course, but he hasn't been healthy and effective at the same time since 2024. That's awfully risky.

Evans is a quality second piece as long as he bounces back well from Tommy John surgery. He made his MLB debut with the Mariners in 2025 and underwhelmed (4.32 ERA with iffy underlying numbers in 81 ⅓ innings), though he was regarded as a strong prospect before that, someone who should hold down a rotation spot for a long time.

Here's what FanGraphs wrote about Evans in June 2025, the last time he was prospect-eligible:

(His) sweeper is easily his best pitch, spins in at 2,800 rpm, and has hellacious lateral wipe. His reliance on it robs it of some bat-missing ability, and the last couple of years, the miss rate on Evans' slider has been pretty average because he's so often trying to throw it for strikes and hitters anticipate its arrival. But because Evans' fastball is fairly vulnerable, he's forced to lean on his breaking stuff ... Again, it's really only the sweeper that's plus, but Evans has a super deep repertoire, he throws a good rate of strikes and gets groundballs, and in 2024, he proved he could sustain this kind of stuff across more than 100 innings. Without a single pitch generating plus miss, he's probably not going to be a star, but he does enough to be a useful member of a big league rotation in a no. 4/5 capacity.

The Royals will have to wait for Evans to make an impact in their uniform because the timing of his Tommy John surgery means his rehab will extend into next spring and summer, but he is a quality second piece even if he is only a No. 4-5 starter. Cheap back-end starters are incredibly valuable and Evans should be that once his elbow is ready to go.

Ferrer could very well wind up closing games for the Royals this season and is a quality add to the bullpen. For Kansas City, the trade boils down to three things. One, can they keep Miller healthy and get him back to his 2024 form? He's the headliner in the trade and his success is imperative. Two, will Evans turn into a reliable rotation member once his elbow is sound?

And three, was Nick Loftin's 2026 for real? The Royals believe it was, hence trading Garcia. Loftin, 28, was a Gold Glove finalist this past season and he authored a .240/.322/.388 batting line with eight home runs in 118 games. If you're sold on Loftin as a league-average hitter and Gold Glove-caliber defender, well, that's what Garcia is, just without the name value.

The Royals badly needed rotation help -- there's no arguing that -- but they also ranked 22nd in runs this year and were middle of the pack defensively despite Loftin's (and Garcia's) glovework. There's a chance Kansas City made its position player core worse with only unspectacular pitching upgrades to show for it. I understand what they did. I just don't love it.

Green Bay has won 11 of the 18 regular-season meetings between the teams, but Ryan Fitzgerald's 49-yard field goal at the end of the fourth quarter gave the Panthers a 16-13 victory at Lambeau last year.
