#2548. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 12

The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column, this WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position will be updated here soon.

1. Ja'Marr Chase (vs. NO) - 93.5 proj. receiving yards

Chase had a disappointing Week 11 in a good match. Some of that was not coming down with his deep target. Some of that was the rain. A lot of it was Joe Burrow having an off night against a chaotic defense. It happens. He's still the WR1 on WR4 usage this month and the WR4 across the year.

The Saints have done a decent job on underneath passes but have allowed others to win downfield. There's no reason for the Bengals to move off of their league-leading 67% neutral pass rate here. Cincy has a 30.25-point team total (second).

2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at SF) - 97.5 proj. receiving yards

Smith-Njigba is the WR2 in per-game half PPR scoring on WR6 expected-points usage over his past four games with Drew Lock and Sam Darnold splitting time. He has topped 100 receiving yards in three of those four contests while drawing a 44% target share in that span. What's new?

San Francisco ranks 11th in half PPR points allowed per game to opposing wideouts, having surrendered 71.2 fantasy points to the Cowboys receiver room in Week 10 when chasing points. JSN has tons of experience against this defense, most recently posting 118, 19, 84, 124 and 118 yards. Seattle travels as 3-point road underdogs with a 21.75-point team total (17th). Throwing the ball to the perimeter is the best way to move the ball against the Niners, in my opinion.

3. CeeDee Lamb (vs. PHI) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb is the WR3 on WR2 usage this year, ranking second in targets per game (11.8) and third in yards per game (100.7). Through 11 weeks of an NFL season, Lamb's 208.2 half PPR points are 13th all-time. All-time.

The Eagles have been bad against Lamb-type receivers all year and now won't have All Pro LB Zack Baun. They've allowed the third-most points to fantasy WRs, and Lamb finished as the WR5 on WR1 overall usage against them in Week 7. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites.

4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. CHI) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards

St. Brown is having his usual season. He's the WR5 on WR7 usage, after going on a touchdown-less rut throughout October.

This matchup has the potential for a blowup game. The biggest factor will be if slot CB Kyler Gordon can play after he missed last week. The Bears have been pretty woeful in the secondary beyond him, while shutting down the run since Jeffery Simmons appeared. The Sun God was the WR5 and WR1 in matchups against them last year, both wins for Detroit. Jaxon Smith-Njigba hung 118-1 against them in Week 8 in a similar role, too. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs carrying a 26.5-point implied team total (sixth).

5. Justin Jefferson (vs. ATL) - 84.5 proj. receiving yards

Jefferson is the WR18 on WR8 usage over the past two weeks with Kirk Cousins. The fumble on that in-cut explosion was a real bummer, but that completion had a lot of timing and anticipation from the QB, something Jefferson hasn't had since 2023. He had plenty of breaking routes against the 49ers, and Kevin O'Connell drew up two different downfield shots to him, too. A big game is long overdue. The signs of it happening soon are there.

This is a sweet matchup for just that. The Falcons don't have Pro Bowl FS Jessie Bates, and CB1 A.J. Terrell is having a down season in isolation. The Vikings getting their OL healthy again would be nice, but Jefferson should have room to operate either way. The Falcons have allowed the fifth-most passing yards per game this year and the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs. Minnesota has a strong 24.75-point team total, and Jordan Addison (finger) isn't expected to play.

6. Parker Washington (vs. TEN) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards

That really should've been a touchdown. Come on, refs! Washington still was a top-20 WR last week and is now the WR13 on WR12 usage across the season. He can be up-and-down based on the Jaguars' lopsided history, but when games are tighter, Washington catches fire, as he did last week when he racked up 16 targets while trailing.

This week, the Jaguars are expected to go crazy on offense. They have a league-high 31.0-point team total against the Titans, who have allowed 362 passing yards per game over the past month. Read that again. And again. It's one of the wildest stats of the year. It doesn't take a genius to feel good about Washington's ceiling odds here. He had 152-1 against them just two weeks ago.

7. Tee Higgins (vs. NO) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins was only targeted three times in last week's disappointing upset loss. It happens at WR, even for the top options. Higgins' best games are likely behind him, but he is the WR7 on WR20 usage this year. His worst-case scenario is returning back to the WR1/2 border as the season closes. The schedule is light enough to dream higher than that.

The Saints have allowed the fourth-most points on 15+ air yard targets to WRs. That's the clear upside path he needs in a rebound spot. The Bengals have a 30.25-point team total (second).

8. George Pickens (vs. PHI) - 70.5 proj. receiving yards

We're so back. Pickens has 38.0 and 20.3 half PPR points, respectively, in his two games since the bye. He had one of the best grabs of the year last week along the sideline, while Dak Prescott had all day to pass behind a great Cowboys OL. It's an environment for Pickens to have monster games, even if his role and style come with some volatility. He's at his best when teams go to single high coverage, something the Eagles typically don't do.

That said, CB1 Quinyon Mitchell is dealing with a new hamstring injury, and the other star players won't be available with Jordan Davis on the Jaguars and LB Zack Baun on IR. Mitchell's status is a big deal for Pickens' matchup. Across the season, the Eagles have had far too many blown coverages, leading to the third-most fantasy points allowed to WRs (31.3). Pickens had 57-1 against them in Week 7 and 146-1 against them late last year. Dallas carries a 28-point team total (fourth) as 8.5-point home favorites.

9. Malik Nabers (at IND) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

Nabers had a handful of underneath receptions against elite CB1 Travis Hunter last week, then teleported into the back of the end zone against Jacksonville's nickel defender to bring Nabers to a top-15 WR finish. Since Week 4, Nabers is the WR9 on WR4 usage with Puka Nacua as one of the receivers ahead. Things will always be up-and-down with J.J. McCarthy, who missed him way out of bounds for a potential back-shoulder TD, but Nabers is way too good to not be treated as a fantasy WR1 now.

The Giants have a healthy 24.0-point team total this week, and that'll easily be one of their best all year. The Colts are tanking and have allowed the 10th-most passing yards per game over their last four games. We'll see if CB1 Sauce Gardner or CB2 Charvarius Ward will return this week. Nico Collins had an awesome deep touchdown against their backups last week, and Nabers had a 171-2 game against the Colts during his rookie season, for what it's worth. Long story short, Nabers looks great this week.

10. Nico Collins (vs. BAL) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins ranks as the WR18 in half PPR points per game on WR31 expected-points usage across his last four appearances. His weekly target volume has fluctuated wildly, bottoming out at four targets in two separate contests while spiking to 15 targets in Week 10 against Cleveland. The good news is the Texans have recently ramped his snap rates up out of desperation and with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jaylen Noel sidelined. Collins is the WR11 on WR20 usage this year. That's a fair range for him. A long dunk-on-you TD made him the WR18 last week.

Baltimore's defense has underwhelmed. We'll see if podcaster Marlon Humphrey is back this week, but he's been bad this year anyway. Collins will likely see a bunch of CB1 Nate Wiggins, who has the speed to match with Collins downfield. Opponents facing the Ravens have posted a 46% neutral pass rate, the third-lowest rate in the NFL and the Texans are 6.5-point home favorites. He likely won't have that many targets here, but a 26.5-point team total (seventh) suggests he'll be a big reason why that is.

11. Matthew Golden (at LAR) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden has produced as the WR8 in half PPR points per game on WR5 expected-points usage over his last four games. The breakout sophomore has commanded a 33% target share alongside 10.8 targets and 133 air yards per game, topping nine targets in all four contests. These are the type of metrics that make the drops livable. Golden is one of the best separators in the NFL. Full stop.

The Rams present a stingy draw on paper, ranking 30th in half PPR points allowed to WRs (21.5 per game). Opposing offenses have largely avoided testing them through the air, but have CB2 Jaylen Watson on IR right now, at least. Golden may see a handful of Trent McDuffie in this one, so he may not be as open as he usually is. The Packers simply don't have other avenues to move the ball, so Golden should still see plenty of looks. Green Bay is listed as 3-point road underdogs with a 20.75-point team total (19th).

12. Christian Watson (at LAR) - 75.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson is the WR7 on WR16 usage this season, while the past month has cooled off (WR15 on WR28 usage). He's already faced the Vikings twice and the Bucs this year, and he's been masterful in the other contests. Green Bay won't have Josh Jacobs and will need its signature splash plays to win on Thanksgiving Eve on the road.

The Rams have been tough on WRs, ranking 30th in half PPR points allowed to the position at 21.5 per game. They also sit 27th against deep passes over 15 air yards, allowing only 6.3 points per game on downfield attempts. Their structure is to stop this aerial offense, but easier said than done. CB2 Jaylen Watson being on IR certainly helps Watson's odds. Green Bay travels as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20.75 points (19th).

13. Mike Evans (vs. SEA) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

Removing screens, Evans is the WR1 overall in yards per route (4.1) this season as a 33-year-old grown man. He's been a total monster at the catch point as usual, and the 49ers are often in the red zone to take advantage of his size and ball tracking. He's the WR12 on WR19 usage throughout the year, including his injured games. He put up 109 yards against the dang Vikings in Mexico City last week and his best game of the year was against the Seahawks. He doesn't care about matchups.

Speaking of, it's rematch SZN with Evans taking on Seattle at home here. He dunked all over CB2 Josh Jobe in Week 5, when he was the WR6 on WR5 usage. That's largely been the only great game at receiver against the Seahawks all year, with nobody posting more than 60 yards at WR since. The 49ers have a 24.75-point team total, which is a sign of respect to the Hawks defense. San Francisco is averaging 31.6 points per game.

14. Garrett Wilson (at MIA) - 59.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll see if Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) can return later on. Wilson is used a little less often when the entire skill room is healthy. He's been the WR25 on WR17 usage this year, through no fault of his own. He's the WR3 overall in ESPN's on-field tracking metrics, and I've seen him wide open way too often on inaccurate passes. He's turned 12.8 expected points per game into 8.1 points this month. That does make him a positive regression candidate, though we've said that for his entire career.

The Dolphins have quietly been great against fantasy WRs, only allowing 21.6 half PPR points per game to WR rooms (29th). Part of that is that first-round rookie CB Chris Johnson is turning into a real player already. DJ Moore was able to do some damage in matchups away from Johnson last week, however, finishing with 91 yards and a score.

15. Jameson Williams (vs. CHI) - 56.5 proj. receiving yards

Jamo is one of a kind. Only he can front flip into the end zone one week after Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL celebrating with a jump. The good news is not that he landed it (he didn't); it's that he keeps finding the end zone. He's the WR20 on WR34 usage this season now. Jared Goff is dynamite right now and was able to hang in the pocket to deliver a strike to Jamo on his post TD. He's only averaging 3.6 receptions per game this year, but he certainly makes them count as usual.

This matchup is a dreamy one. The Bears have been nuked on double moves and go balls by outside speed receivers this year. They've allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs on 15+ air-yard throws, while limiting underneath receivers with slot CB Kyler Gordon (questionable) as their top corner. Williams has been the WR20, WR10 and WR4 in his most recent games against them. The Lions are a rare underdog here, yet still have a 26.5-point team total (fifth) in what is obviously a potential shoutout.

16. Luther Burden III (at DET) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

Burden is going to be very volatile in this role. He only played 12 of 27 snaps with multiple TEs on the field, playing behind Rome Odunze and Kalif Raymond. The Bears love his YAC ability but don't trust him in all ways at the moment. That's part of the reason why he's an All-Pro in first halves and goes away in second halves. Burden is the WR21 on WR42 usage in games with Caleb Williams this season on a team-high 22% target share.

This is a matchup to be very excited about, especially if CB1 D.J. Reed can't suit up in the secondary. The Lions won't have DE1 and LB1, and they have already been averaging 254 passing YPG (fourth most) as a pass funnel. A team total of 29.0 points (third) with the division on the line are the cherries on top.

17. Chris Olave (at CIN) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave has been the WR20 on WR11 usage in his three games with Jordyn Tyson. He bottomed out two weeks ago in a downfield role, then rebounded to 14 targets while chasing points to the Bears. Tyson was a part-time player again, only playing a fracture of their heavier sets. Olave is too talented to not be heavily featured in a struggling offense, and there is little skillset overlap between he and the rookie. Olave >>> Tyson on tape to me.

The Bengals are a difficult matchup for top outside WRs, dating back years. Part of that is because extremely quick CB1 D.J. Turner is excellent (aside from covering Antonio Williams last MNF). Part of that is the rest of the back half is more mediocre, so the ball should go to slots and TEs. The Bengals have allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy points to WRs on 15+ air yard throws, where Olave breads his butter. Some adjustments are needed, but the fact that the fast-paced Saints are 10-point dogs baked in a very high projected dropback total.

18. Zay Flowers (at HOU) - 66.5 proj. receiving yards

The Ravens have 89 dropbacks in their two games with Jacoby Brissett, the most over that stretch. There's more than enough volume to go around for Flowers to hold the fantasy WR2 line. He's been the WR11 and WR35 in usage in those two games, seeing 11 targets for 8-97-0. There will be fewer downfield shots completed compared to the peak Lamar Jackson MVP era, and that's the difference between being a top-8 option and being down here.

On paper, the Texans are an easy matchup, but I don't buy it. They've tightened it up recently, only allowing 23.6 half PPR points per game to WRs over the past month. They held down the Colts, Browns and Chargers, while Malik Nabers hung 111 receiving yards back in Week 7. Nabers is a good stylistic comp for Flowers, so there's still a path to a ceiling even with this strong secondary. Baltimore enters as 6.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20 points (22nd).

19. Drake London (at MIN) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

London hasn't cleared 16.5 half PPR points since Week 3 when Michael Penix debuted. They've been on the struggle bus recently, bottoming out as the WR30 on WR22 usage this past month on a 25% target share. They forgot how to complete the forward pass against the Bucs three games ago, but London was the WR15 on season-high usage (WR8) before their bye against a strong Chiefs defense. Hopefully they can settle down Penix coming out of the off week.

Penix facing the Brian Flores chaos has everyone nervous. The Falcons could try to run the ball early before peppering underneath targets to make sure Penix doesn't panic against the most blitz heavy defense in NFL history. Atlanta's offense has recorded a 44% neutral pass rate (31st), while Minnesota's defense has allowed a 46% neutral pass rate (31st). Atlanta enters as 6.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 17.5 points (28th). It's hard to find the string to pull on based on the matchup. The good news is fellow giant Mike Evans was just the WR4 against this defense last week. That was also an outlier performance in another country at an altitude we can't relate to.

20. DeVonta Smith (at DAL) - 64.5 proj. receiving yards

Smith is going to be chasing air yards and expected fantasy points the rest of the season with Joe Milton at QB. There's an accuracy problem to all levels of the field. Smith was missed on a couple of out routes, on an out-and-up along the sideline and on a potential 69-yard go ball. Smith finished as the WR40 on WR11 usage. The good news is he looked healthy, and the defense is in a bad spot, so there will be game script on his side often.

The matchup with the Cowboys is a bit more challenging with CB1 Joey Porter Jr. healthy again, but they have been hilariously bad all year for a million reasons. Calvin Ridley and Carnell Tate had wild scores against this unit last week, and it was 109-2 for Deebo Samuel the week prior. They find new ways to be embarrassed. And still, the Eagles have a 19.5-point team total (23rd).

21. DJ Moore (vs. KC) - 50.5 proj. receiving yards

Moore is going overlooked because of all the partial games earlier in the season. He's the WR13 in yards per route, removing screens. He's also the WR12 on WR16 usage this past month after returning from injury. He's winning on run-away routes, and the Bills will move him around, too. It's been a great marriage into the offense. Moore had the best breaking-route tape of his season just last week, ultimately scoring a red-zone touchdown on the backside of a Josh Allen progression. A 23% target share on a great offense is a great place to be with his YAC ability. He had a season-high 17.0 expected half PPR points last week.

The Chiefs are a very real test for Moore in every way. Albeit against an easy schedule, Kansas City is second-best against fantasy WRs this season, allowing the second-fewest points on 15+ air yard targets where Moore is the most lethal. Offenses facing the Chiefs have run the ball at the highest rate in neutral situations (46%), likely to stay away from this awesome cornerback duo of Nohl Williams and first-round rookie Mansoor Delane. Both are very physical when fully healthy. Allen is far more experienced against a menacing Steve Spagnuolo defense, but few have got it done at receiver against them so far. JSN was the outlier when he hung 163 yards on them. Buffalo enters the week as 3-point home favorites with a strong 26.75-point team total (fifth).

22. Tetairoa McMillan (at TB) - 60.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan ranks as the WR24 in half PPR points per game on WR17 expected points across his last four appearances, seeing between 10.3 and 14.3 expected half PPR points in all of them. He's seen a solid 25% target share during that span, icing Jalen Coker. In 21 games alongside Jalen Coker since 2025, he has averaged 9.9 half PPR points and 7.0 targets per game. Consider that his low-end baseline.

The Bucs defense has been one of the standout units throughout the year, though the Lions and Bears have moved the ball well against them of late. Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown scored TDs against backup CB2 Benjamin Morrison right after impressive CB2 Jacob Parrish (back) left. It's a big deal for T-Mac, as he'd certainly see a lot of Parrish here. There's still CB1 Zyon McCollum to worry about, but the matchup just softened and the Panthers will likely be forced into more dropbacks as this historically has been a pass funnel with DT Vita Vea clogging it up the gut. When these teams met in Week 7, McMillan caught four of six targets for 40 scoreless yards. He was the WR19 and WR13 against them last year. The Panthers enter Monday night as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (21st).

23. Denzel Boston (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Boston's downfield role is the most volatile in the Browns' pass game, and we've felt the worst of that of late. He's the WR62 on WR21 usage this past month, a very clear sign that he's a positive regression candidate waiting to score a longer touchdown. Last week was a season-low 4.5 expected half PPR points for what it's worth. He's had the Post-Bye Rookie Bump to work out the kinks. His film has been very good. It's just about having the QB play and game script cooperating all at once.

The matchup is excellent. The Raiders have allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to WRs this past month. Over the entire year, they've allowed the most production on WR targets 15+ air yards downfield, where Boston specializes. The Browns are 4.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 23 points (15th). There are reasons to buy low here as a boom-bust WR3.

24. Rome Odunze (at DET) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Odunze is the WR33 on WR42 usage since Week 6 when Caleb Williams returned. He's not getting the volume of a must-start WR3, but Odunze is a downfield and red-zone threat in an awesome offense. If he can secure the ball cleanly, there will be a massive game from him down the stretch here.

The matchup is a great one, with the Lions allowing the fourth-most passing yards per game. It'll get even better if CB1 D.J. Reed (hip) can't play again. This unit has allowed the 11th-most fantasy points to WRs on 15+ air yard targets, and that will be a lot easier with a backup corner on Odunze. Back in Week 2 of last year, Odunze had 128 yards and two scores against this defense. That was his best game in terms of targets (11), receptions (seven) and fantasy points (28.3 half PPR). The Bears enter as 2.5-point road favorites with a 29-point team total (third).

Williams had his break out game on Monday Night Football, capped by two dagger explosives on the game-winning drive. The last one was in man coverage against CB1 D.J. Turner, who is a top-10 CB in my eyes. He has more juice than expected while playing on the perimeter. These are the type of plays to get very excited about as the Commanders look for their long-term WR1 for Jayden Daniels. He's up to WR34 on WR37 usage over the past month with Terry McLaurin on IR. That's the Post-Bye Rookie Bump for you.

A date with the Cardinals adds fuel to the fire. They've been 10th-worst against the position this year, specifically allowed the eighth-most fantasy points to the 5-20 air yard window that Williams has been the best in. To their credit, Arizona has tightened up this month, but Washington still travels to the desert as 7-point road favorites carrying an implied team total of 24.25 points (10th).

26. Stefon Diggs (at ARI) - 46.5 proj. receiving yards

Diggs faces pressure from impressive Day two rookie Antonio Williams, but his slot role is safe as long as he keeps making plays. It was actually Jayden Daniels who held him back from a bigger Week 11, as the QB missed him open in the end zone. Diggs is still the WR24 on WR24 usage this season, averaging a 22% target share over the past month. 73% of his targets have come under 10 air yards this year, so he'll need some YAC moments, a ton of volume or a red zone touchdown to find a ceiling path.

This is an eruption against the Cardinals. The Commanders are listed as 7-point road favorites with an implied team total of 24.25 points (10th).

27. Rashee Rice (at BUF) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Rice isn't going to reach his top-10 fantasy WR status in this new role, but he's held the line as a fantasy WR2/3. Over the past month since his injury, Rice is the WR28 on WR36 usage with Josh Downs now involved on similar intermediate routes. He's had a 20% target share this month with a 5.6 aDOT. The Chiefs opted for a WR-by-committee last week to make sure Xavier Worthy, Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong got snaps, too. Rice played 22-of-39 receiving snaps (56%) through three quarters. We'll see if he keeps getting the occasional deep target as he's had recently. That'd be his best way to add the occasional spike week.

The Bills are weakest through the air, though new S1 Amani Hooker is going to shore things up moving forward. They've allowed the 14th-most fantasy points to WRs this year and CB1 Christian Benford hasn't played recently. If he can't go, there is a clear opportunity for all WRs. Rice had 86-1 against Buffalo last year for what it's worth. The Chiefs enter Thanksgiving as 3-point road underdogs with an implied total of 23.75 points (11th).

28. KC Concepcion (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

#2547. Tuesday's CIAC football playoff update: Newtown among four to unofficially qualify for CIAC playoffs, 14 berths remain

Four more teams unofficially clinched CIAC football playoff berths Tuesday night, according to GametimeCT projections, bringing the statewide total to 34 as Thanksgiving Week's football schedule got underway.

That leaves 14 playoff berths up for grabs heading into Wednesday's games. Our projections are determined using the CIAC playoff formula, using OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna medium model and verified by GametimeCT using the current CIAC football playoff standings.

The points are not official until the CIAC football playoff committee meets and approves the final tally the day after all the games are completed on Thanksgiving Day.

In, CLASS LL, FAIRFIELD PREP (6-4) clinched with its 38-15 victory over Xavier, narrowing the available spots to three, mainly between NFA, Hamden, and South Windsor, though Glastonbury and the winner of Stamford-Westhill remained mathematically alive.

LEWIS MILLS/WOLCOTT TECH (8-2) earned its first state playoff berth in school history with its 17-0 victory over Avon/St. Paul, leaving three spots available.

In CLASS MM, NEWTOWN (7-2) clinched when Xavier lost to Fairfield Prep, leaving three spots available. Despite the loss, XAVIER (6-4) remains alive but now needs help - namely two of Platt, Torrington or Wilton to lose, or it'll be in trouble.

TORRINGTON (6-3) and PLATT (6-3) can now clinch with wins on Thanksgiving. WILTON (5-4) needs to win and get help. NEW MILFORD (6-4) remained mathematically alive with its 34-6 Candlewood Cup victory over New Fairfield, but is a longshot to steal a spot.

THAMES RIVER CO-OP (8-2) failed to clinch a home playoff game with its 20-7 loss to Montville/St. Bernard and will now await other results to improve its positioning.

VALLEY REGIONAL/OLD LYME (7-3) clinched by virtue of its 47-28 victory over Haddam-Killingworth in the Principal's Cup, simultaneously eliminating Haddam-Killingworth.

Also, TOLLAND's 29-7 victory over E.O. Smith clinched the Eagles a home quarterfinal. MONTVILLE/ST. BERNARD (6-4) remained alive with its 20-7 victory over Thames River co-op.

There are 17 games scheduled for Wednesday, including several moved up to avoid rainy weather forecasts on Thanksgiving morning.

Among some of the big games with playoff implications:

Woodland (6-3) at Seymour (6-3), 6 p.m. - The winner clinches in Class S, while the loser will be relying on outside help to clinch.

Holy Cross (8-1) at Wolcott (6-3), 6 p.m.

- Wolcott must beat Holy Cross to stay alive in the Class S race. Losing will help the other contenders. Holy Cross is looking to improve its seeding in Class MM.

Coginchaug co-op (6-3) at North Branford (9-0), 6 p.m. - Coginchaug must beat the unbeaten T-Birds to clinch a spot in Class S, or hope outside results go its way. North Branford is already the No. 1 seed in the class.

Fairfield Warde (6-3) at Fairfield Ludlowe (9-0), 6 p.m. - Warde has an outside shot at a Class L berth, but it must beat unbeaten Ludlowe, which is vying for a top seed in the class.

Rockville (7-2) at Ellington (5-4), 6:30 p.m. - Ellington must win to keep its playoff hopes alive in Class M heading into Thanksgiving morning. Then it will need Waterford to lose to 1-8 East Lyme. Rockville's hoping to get a quarterfinal home game with a win coupled with a Guilford loss.

Guilford (7-2) at Hand (9-0), 7 p.m. - Guilford can clinch a home game in Class M, but it hasn't beaten the Tigers since 2006. Hand is already the No. 1 seed in class SS.

South Windsor (4-5) at Enfield (2-7), 6 p.m. - The Bobcats must win to get in line for a Class LL playoff spot. It still needs help, specifically a Hamden loss on Thanksgiving.

Farmington (6-3) at Plainville (9-0), 6 p.m. - Farmington needs to beat unbeaten Plainville to stay alive in Class L while Plainville is hoping to clinch the No. 2 seed in SS with its first unbeaten season in 80 years.

Xavier's loss to Fairfield Prep relieved Newtown of playoff pressure heading into this game. Both teams hope to improve their seeding. For Newtown, a home playoff game. For Masuk, potentially the No. 1 seed in the Class M playoffs.

#2546. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

#2545. MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal hosts more meetings, Red Sox add backup catcher, plus Padres, Phillies, Rays, more

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The hot stove is starting to heat up. On Tuesday, David Bednar and Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer while Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe, Adrian Morejon, Trevor Rogers, and Seiya Suzuki declined it. Those five are now attached to draft pick compensation. Also, the White Sox landed righty Dustin May on a three-year contract.

We're still waiting on the offseason's first real blockbuster but things are beginning to pick up. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Wednesday's hot stove happenings.

The Red Sox have acquired catcher Nick Fortes from the AL East rival Rays for 17-year-old minor-league righty Angel Roa, the team announced on Wednesday. Fortes will take over as Adley Rutschman's backup catcher. He is projected to make $3.4 million or so through arbitration in 2027, which is a pricey sum for a backup catcher, particularly for a small payroll team like the Rays. Connor Wong has been designated for assignment by the Red Sox in a corresponding move.

Fortes, 30, had a career-best season at the plate in 2026, though his defensive numbers took a big dip. The Rays acquired Liam Hicks at the trade deadline and he is their clear-cut starting catcher. Kenny Piper, who made his MLB debut in August, could step in as the backup until top prospect Caden Bodine is ready, which could be as soon as next summer.

The Blue Jays and Dodgers had in-person meetings with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Tuesday, reports ESPN. He will meet with the Padres later this week and already met with the Mets on Monday. Rival executives expect it to come down to Blue Jays and Mets, per ESPN. Toronto has a history of pursuing top free agents but missing out (Shohei Ohtani, Kyle Tucker, etc.).

Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Scott Boras clients. The Dodgers are said to have interest in a short-term contract with a large annual salary, something that is unlikely to appeal to Skubal. He's poised to land a record contract for a pitcher, perhaps even more than $400 million.

Star shortstop Corey Seager has expressed an openness to a trade to only a "handful of teams," reports ESPN. Seager has a full no-trade clause and can pick his destination, and was reportedly quite picky as a free agent five years ago. The Rangers are open to trading Seager, as well as Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi, who also have full no-trade protection. deGrom already reportedly invoked his no-trade clause at last season's deadline to spike a deal to the Braves.

Seager, 33 in April, had surgery to remove a bone spur from his elbow last month, and was limited to 102 games by injuries in 2026. When healthy, he has typically beibeeng very good, but the injuries and surgeries are mounting. Seager is owed $31 million annually through 2031. Texas would likely have to eat some money to facilitate a trade.

On Tuesday, the Padres hosted free agent outfielder Seiya Suzuki for a recruiting visit, according to ESPN. San Diego aggressively pursued Suzuki when he initially came over from Japan five years ago, but he opted to sign with the Cubs instead. We ranked Suzuki as the seventh-best free agent available this offseason, and the third-best free agent position player.

San Diego needs rotation help more than anything this offseason, though they could use another middle-of-the-lineup bat as well. They could sign Suzuki, plant him in right field, and move Fernando Tatis Jr. back to the infield, where he played 53 games at second base this past season. It was Tatis' first action on the infield since he was the team's starting shortstop in 2021.

After signing Jake Bauers, president of baseball operations Craig Breslow said it is "hard to envision that there's something significant on the horizon" for the Red Sox, according to the Boston Globe. That doesn't mean the Red Sox won't do something significant later in the offseason, perhaps after the lockout, but, right now, there is nothing major in the works.

Breslow's next order of business is unclogging his outfield/DH logjam, which could involve trading or even non-tendering Jarren Duran. The Red Sox also have four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, John Oviedo) and could trade from that depth. Otherwise, Boston has no glaring roster issues remaining this offseason.

Free agent slugger Randy Arozarena is seeking well over $100 million and could end up waiting until after the lockout to sign, according to ESPN. For now, teams are balking at that asking price, but that isn't unusual this early in the offseason. The Orioles and Yankees are among the clubs reported to have interest in Arozarena, our ninth-ranked free agent.

Although Arozarena had the better 2026 season, Suzuki is considered the more desirable free agent because he's a much better defender. They're roughly the same age and are comparable hitters, but Arozarena is a borderline DH at this point. Right-handed power is in shockingly short supply, though. He (and Suzuki) would improve almost any lineup. As noted above, both players declined the qualifying offer from their respective teams, which means they are tagged with draft pick compensation.

The Phillies are receiving trade calls about righty reliever Orion Kerkering, reports The Athletic. Kerkering struggled badly in the second half, allowing 25 runs and 43 baserunners in his final 19 ⅓ MLB innings of the season. The Phillies optioned him to Triple-A a week before the end of the regular season and did not carry him on their Wild Card Series roster.

Still only 25, Kerkering has a history of missing bats at a high level and experience in late-inning situations. He will remain under team control through 2029. The Phillies certainly don't have to trade him. They could keep him and even send him to Triple-A next season. It never hurts to listen, however, and other teams presumably see Kerkering as a buy-low candidate.

Veteran righty Frankie Montas hit 98 mph and wowed scouts during a workout in Arizona this week, reports The Athletic. Multiple general managers were in attendance, and it's possible Montas will land a guaranteed major-league contract. He is rehabbing from Tommy John surgery and has not pitched in an MLB game since August 2025.

Pitching is always in demand, especially cheap pitching with upside behind league-average innings. Montas, 34 in March, has not been healthy and effective at the same time since 2022, though he looked good during his showcase and he has a reputation for being an excellent teammate who mentors young pitchers. That will only help his case.

#2544. New manager, fresh hope. But why the stats say Al Faisaly don't need overhaul

Mohamed Dahman replaces Giovanni Solinas in the dugout ahead of his debut match against fellow new boys Diriyah Club

It might seem a rather obvious statement, but football is all about goals.

The important distinction, however, is it is just as important to deny them as it is to score them. Just look at promoted sides Al Faisaly and Diriyah Club.

Both started the 2026-27 Roshn Saudi League with different expectations and ambitions. Yet despite Diriyah Club signing Darwin Nunez, it is actually Al Faisaly that has scored the more goals this season out of the two - 13 goals to 10.

The issue is, though, that Al Faisaly have conceded almost twice as many (24 to 13) and that is the story of their respective campaigns so far.

Mohamed Dahman takes temporary charge of Al Faisaly following Giovanni Solinas' resignation

There is much to like in how the Al Majma'ah-based side have played and, although manager Giovanni Solinas recently resigned, his interim replacement, Mohamed Dahman, inherits a squad that is already halfway there.

At present, Al Faisaly are the league's No.1-ranked pressing team, applying high-pressure to 46.3 percent of opposition touches, yet their opponents complete 79.2% of passes under that pressure.

The former is proof they have the style right; they now just need to increase its effectiveness. That is, forcing more errors and turning the ball over more often. That's easier said than done, of course, but it's a better place to start than the alternative.

Giovanni Solinas leaves Al Faisaly with the club one spot above the relegation zone

The key focus for Dahman against Diriyah Club when the two RSL new boys meet in Matchweek 13 on Thursday must be on how the hosts start the game. That's because the statistics reveal that Al Faisaly have conceded a league-high number of goals (14) in the first half.

Drilling down even further, 13 of those have been conceded in the opening 30 minutes - also a league high - and eight between minutes 16 and 30. That latter? You guessed it, a league high.

Contrast that to Diriyah Club, who are yet to give away a goal in the opening 15 minutes, and have conceded only six in the first half, and the contrast hits home.

"We exploited the opposition's defensive confusion after the first goal," explained Al Fayha coach Fabio Carille late last month, after his team's Sudair Derby success against Al Faisaly.

So, for Al Faisaly, tightening their belts defensively must be priority No.1. That said, it's not through lack of effort: they sit second for tackles and third for interceptions in the RSL this season.

They're pressing high, they're winning tackles and intercepting the ball but, despite all of that, they still have the league's third-worst defensive record.

Yet it's not all bad news. There are plenty of positives that can give Al Faisaly cause for optimism heading into the Buraidah clash with Diriyah Club.

Chief among those is the threat provided by the crossing ability of Yassen Barnawi, who has recorded a league-high successful crosses from open play (13).

Al Faisaly take on an upwardly mobile Diriyah Club, lead by on-loan star Darwin Nunez

What makes that so threatening is the fact that five of Al Faisaly's 13 goals (38%) have been headers - again ranked No.1 across the league. With almost a third of Diriyah Club's goals conceded this term being headers, that offers a unique opportunity to exploit.

In fact, this is something opposition managers are already aware of, with Carille commenting before the Sudair Derby: "We watched [Al Faisaly's] previous match against Abha, and we know how dangerous their crosses are."

In that, they also have the perfect focal point to get on the end of it in Alexandre Mendy, who has five goals in the RSL and ranks sixth in the division for total shots (19).

Summer signing Alexandre Mendy has five goals in 12 RSL games for Al Faisaly

That backs up the fact Al Faisaly have more goals than Diriyah Club through the opening 12 rounds. Also, it illustrates that they are generating and scoring enough, relatively speaking, when they attack.

And, as noted, it only amplifies the need to tighten up defensively.

Do that and the four draws they've had could easily have been turned into wins. Still, with seven points in their past four games, there is enough to believe 15th-placed Al Faisaly aren't far away from flipping their fortunes.

Thursday, against a fellow promoted side albeit with different aspirations, represents a decent place to start.

#2543. Mike McCarthy backed Aaron Rodgers as Steelers QB. He benched him a day later.

Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy looked almost confused the question had been asked.

A reporter at McCarthy's Monday, Nov. 23 news conference asked the first-year coach if he'd consider playing a quarterback other than Aaron Rodgers, the veteran in the final year of his career.

McCarthy, who also spent 13 seasons with Rodgers in Green Bay, left little doubt about his feelings while declaring Rodgers was the team's QB. Take a look:

Then, in a stunning development late Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Steelers announced quarterback Mason Rudolph will start in Week 12's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos. McCarthy was not scheduled to address reporters again before the Steelers face the Broncos at the time of the announcement about Rodgers.

#2540. Pep Guardiola admits he was 'embarrassed' to reject Italy job as former Man City boss confirms national team management is his 'next step'

Pep Guardiola has broken his silence on his decision to turn down the opportunity to manage Italy, admitting he felt "embarrassed" to say no to the Azzurri. The legendary tactician, currently on a sabbatical following a trophy-laden decade at Manchester City, also confirmed that his next move in football will be onto the international stage.

In July, after Italy missed a third consecutive World Cup, the Italian federation (FIGC) sent Paolo Maldini and Leonardo to approach Guardiola. The offer arrived shortly after he left Manchester City following a 2016–2026 stint yielding six Premier League titles, three FA Cups and a Champions League crown.

Drained by the grind, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager chose a self-imposed sabbatical of at least one year. Italy subsequently re-hired Roberto Mancini, their Euro 2020-winning coach from 2018 to 2023.

Speaking on Romario TV on Tuesday with Brazil legend and former Barcelona team-mate Romario, Guardiola explained why timing scuppered the Italy move. He also confirmed his desire to eventually coach internationally while insisting he remains content away from the touchline.

"This is the first time I speak about this, but yes, I did talk to them," Guardiola said. "I felt embarrassed to say 'no' to Italy, a country like Italy, it would have been one of the greatest honours of my career to coach the Italian national team. But I realised I needed to stop. If they had called two years earlier, I probably would have accepted.

"But when Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, reached out, it was at a point where I simply had to stop. I needed some time for myself. After 18 years as a coach, with matches every three days, week in and week out, there comes a moment when you just have to say 'phew.'"

Identifying "a national team" as his sole unfulfilled coaching ambition - and "that is the next step" for his career - Guardiola stressed he is in no rush to return. "The truth is, I don't know, I really don't know. But for now, I'm doing fine," he added. "If I ever return, it will be because my gut tells me to, and because someone wants me, then I'll go back. But it's been many years, so many matches."

England, managed by Thomas Tuchel, and the Netherlands, who recently hired Xavi, have both been linked with Guardiola, alongside USMNT following Mauricio Pochettino's exit to Manchester United.

At his final press conference, Pochettino called it "the perfect moment to arrive" at the USMNT and urged Guardiola to take the job: "Everything is in the right direction. I think, of course, take [it]. Take it because [Guardiola is] going to find really good people, good players. The player can fit for his style; the National Training Center that wasn't [there] before."

Suitors must remain patient as Guardiola continues his minimum one-year break away from the dugout. Without a set timeline or destination, his eventual return to international management depends entirely on when his instincts tell him he is ready for a new challenge.

#2537. Rob Manfred 'can't imagine' MLB team owners will accept new CBA without a salary cap

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred on Wednesday said club owners are not willing to compromise on their push for a salary cap and floor in their ongoing negotiations with the players union on a new collective bargaining agreement. While Manfred noted there was general room for compromise with the MLBPA, that does not extend to the central matter of the capped system owners want.

"I can't imagine the owners ratifying a deal that does not include a cap and floor," Manfred said while meeting with the press during the ongoing owners meetings in New York, via the Athletic.

"Thirty clubs are 100% unanimous in support of the proposals that have been made," Manfred said later during a news conference at MLB headquarters. "I'm not in a position to speculate about what happens in the event that we don't achieve our overriding objective, which is to get a cap and floor system that addresses the competitive problem that our fans perceive."

It's possible to parse "can't imagine" as a subtle rhetorical hedge. Additionally, Manfred before he was commissioner was the league's lead negotiator. As such, he's quite familiar with the appearance of unyielding resolve as a tactical implement. Thus, the league has tied every other proposed change to the players' acceptance of a cap and floor, and the players through their union have historically shown zero willingness to accept such a system.

"There can be no clearer example of the league's lack of seriousness than their insistence that they will not negotiate over the economics outside of a radical change to the system that would dramatically reduce overall player compensation for all categories of players and strip fundamental rights from players like the ability to have truly guaranteed contracts," MLBPA interim head Bruce Meyer said Wednesday in a statement.

"There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries."

In their most recent substantive proposal to the players, MLB pitched a $258.3 million cap and $180.2 million floor on team payrolls, with those limits to be phased in gradually. Back in June, the league proposed a $245.3 million cap and $171.2 million floor.

The current CBA, which is the accord that governs every aspect of the working relationship between players and clubs in MLB, is set to expire just before midnight on Dec. 1. At that point, the league is expected to lock out the players at the behest of team owners. The lockout will likely not end until a new CBA is agreed to, at least in principle. Owners also locked out the players in 2021, and that lockout lasted 99 days and very nearly ate into the 2022 regular-season schedule.

#2536. ‘Got to be…’ – Maxx Crosby sounds off on Bijan Robinson’s take about the easiest position in the NFL

Las Vegas Raiders DE Maxx Crosby did not appreciate Atlanta Falcons RB Bijan Robinson's take that the edge rusher is the easiest position in the NFL.

Every elite or contending team is looking to build their offence around a world-class QB and their defence around a world-class edge rusher. Defensive players usually play within a system, so the EDGE is the one defender who is designed to be an independent unit responsible for sacking a slow QB.

Unfortunately, the limited scope of the role led to Falcons RB Robinson dismissing the position as the easiest in the NFL, irking standout EDGE Crosby.

Crosby, a former All-Pro EDGE, responded to Robinson's thoughts on 'The Rush Podcast,' justifying their value while tearing down the position Robinson stars in.

"Casual a– take. Look at it like this: who is your highest-paid player (QB)? And who is next (EDGE)? If it were easy to play the position and get one sack a game, why doesn't everybody do it? Out of 1,000 snaps, getting 10 sacks is great. You're considered elite. Running back? You get handed the ball, and you go play football. You run, and you catch. Running back is, easily, got to be the easiest position to play."

It might be easier to be an average EDGE than an average RB, but the top-tier EDGEs are more valuable because of how scarce the talent at the highest level is, compared to productive RBs being more available.

EDGEs also create plays actively detrimental to another team while having longer careers on average than RBs, so Crosby's point cannot be ignored.

Robinson spoke on the St. Brown Podcast, hosted by Lions RB Amon-Ra St. Brown, and shared his harsh take on edge rushers in the NFL.

"I would say D-Line. Edge rusher. You have one job, get past the tackle. You don't have too much responsibility, especially if you're one who has to rush the passer, I would say that's the easiest. One sack a game."

Crosby is on a three-year, $106.5 million contract, earning $35.8 million with the Raiders in the 2026-27 season.

The White Sox also signed a mid-rotation starter while the Red Sox grabbed a first baseman fresh off a World Series title. Is there enough time for a flurry of moves before the owners lock the players out when the CBA expires on Dec. 1?

In theory, there sure is. We can hold out hope, as there has been enough movement to keep belief alive.

It's no secret that the Diamondbacks are willing to trade All-Star second baseman Ketel Marte. A big hurdle might be his 10-and-5 no-trade rights and questions about which teams Marte would approve in a potential deal. Further, the asking price on Arizona's end is "very high," reports FanSided. Still, plenty of teams are said to be interested.

Marte, 33, has five years and $91.75 million left on his deal. He finished third in MVP voting in 2024, was a highly productive All-Star in 2025, but some issues arose in 2026, including several no-shows. He hit .249/.316/.432 (107 OPS+) with 2.5 WAR and some possible clubhouse baggage.

The Mets are planning a Zoom meeting with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the New York Post. This won't have an impact on their pursuit of Tarik Skubal, just in case anyone is curious.

Taira, 27, has been one of the top pitchers in Japan's NPB for years. Last season, in 23 starts, he had a 1.36 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 141 strikeouts in 146 innings. He's had a sub-2.00 ERA four of the last five seasons, with the exception being a 2.40 in 2023.

CBS Sports ranked Taira as the No. 19 free agent available this winter:

Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu announced on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.

Because of the expected lockout, international free agents are working under an artificial Dec. 1 deadline to sign, rather than the normal posting window.

For now, the Mets' rotation starts with Nolan McLean and Christian Scott.

The Cubs' main focus is on pitching, as well it should be after having one of the worst pitching staffs in baseball along with one of the best collections of position-player talent. Still, both corner outfielders (Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki) have hit free agency along with catcher Carson Kelly, so they can't just ignore the offense. On that front, the ballclub has "extensively scouted" Teruaki Sato, according to The Athletic.

Sato has played mostly third base, where the Cubs have Alex Bregman, but also has outfield experience and could simply serve as DH. In 143 games last season in NPB, Sato hit .306/.383/.609 with 40 doubles, 39 home runs and 106 RBI. His strikeout numbers are high, but sometimes that's the price to be paid for top-level power.

CBS Sports ranked Sato as the No. 4 free agent this winter:

He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact issues to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.

After being one of the most disappointing teams in 2026 and having an active general manager, of course the Mariners weren't going to just sit around after one move. Sure enough, Jerry Dipoto told reporters on Wednesday that they are still looking to add a right-handed bat (remember, Randy Arozarena is a free agent) along with a veteran infielder and a left-handed reliever even after acquiring Garcia. And perhaps most importantly, Dipoto insisted that they do have the payroll flexibility to add all of this.

Further, he also said the rotation is set and no other starting pitchers will be moved. So it'll be Logan Gilbert, George Kirby, Bryan Woo, Emerson Hancock and Kade Anderson heading into next season.

Fresh off signing right-handed starter Dustin May, the White Sox are looking to add another starting pitcher "of similar magnitude," reports the Chicago Sun-Times.

Though the White Sox were one of baseball's best stories last season and made the playoffs, the rotation was very thin. Right now, they have Sean Burke, May, Taylor, Davis Martin and Anthony Kay as their top five and are looking to add another of May's ilk. Things are already looking much better.

The Nationals finished third in the majors in runs scored last season, believe it or not. They trailed only the Cubs and Brewers, scoring more than the Dodgers. The problem was that the pitching staff was mostly a mess. As such, it's no surprise they are after starters and The Athletic names three targets: lefty Kris Bubic, righty Brady Singer and Japanese import Kona Takahashi.

Bubic, 29, has battled shoulder and elbow injuries the past two seasons, but the upside was flashed in the first part of 2025. He made the All-Star team and had a 2.55 ERA through 20 starts and 116 ⅓ innings.

The 30-year-old Singer was 6-15 with a 5.85 ERA for the Reds last season in a disaster of a contract year, but he was productive in the previous two seasons.

Takahashi, 29, was 9-7 with a 2.64 ERA, 1.10 WHIP and 118 strikeouts in 143 ⅓ innings in NPB last season.

#2533. Nick Wright’s Patrick Mahomes take gets trolled in his latest NFL quarterback ranking

Nick Wright's latest NFL quarterback rankings sparked a debate, where his Patrick Mahomes take got brutally trolled.

Patrick Mahomes has done a brilliant job in recent weeks to keep a patched-up Kansas City Chiefs afloat by turning back the clock.

He is clearly not ready to relinquish his throne as the quarterback to usurp in this league, but several contenders are gunning for it.

Nick Wright felt that contendership and more after his latest Patrick Mahomes take got trolled by the whole studio.

Wright creates a "Mahomes Mountain" at the end of every gameweek in the NFL, and as the name suggests, it ranks the quarterbacks in the league.

Being named Mahomes Mountain has nothing to do with the ranking of Mahomes, but Wright perhaps took the name a bit too literally in his latest ranking.

Speaking on First Things First, Wright ranked the quarterbacks, and put Mahomes at the top, ahead of Brock Purdy and Joe Burrow in the tier just below.

While Mahomes has undoubtedly been elite again this season, this take didn't go down well with the rest of his studio, who vouched for Purdy to be at the top.

It got so comedic that Wright's own takes were replayed back to him, which he gave when the 49ers completed a dominant win against the Vikings, courtesy of a perfect Purdy performance.

He said at the time that Purdy is the league MVP, which naturally means that he is the best quarterback in the league as well!

Here's what Wright said to justify placing Mahomes at the top: "He was a man who for the 2nd time in his career, just had a 4-game stretch, averaging 300 yards per game, averaging more than 3 touchdowns per game with no turnovers, which has only been done in his career by one other person, Aaron Rodgers."

Wright's previous comments were immediately played back to him, and he played it off as choosing between two elites, saying two things swayed him – Broussard saying Purdy wasn't the MVP, and him saying Purdy was the best quarterback in the NFC.

How that makes sense is left up to the reader, because Wright didn't seem very convinced about it either!

#2531. Luis Castillo trade grades: White Sox give up steady back-end starter to offload salary; Rockies get creative

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Two days after adding Dustin May to their rotation, the Chicago White Sox have subtracted Luis Castillo and Davis Martin. The White Sox are sending Castillo and Martin to the Colorado Rockies for lefty Sean Sullivan and minor-league catcher Douglas Veliz, the teams announced late Thursday. The Rockies will take on Castillo's entire contract.

Castillo, 33, joined the White Sox in a deadline trade with the Seattle Mariners. He struggled badly after the deal, allowing 30 runs in 31 innings, and he finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. Castillo has one year remaining on his contract at $22.75 million, though a $25 million option for 2028 will vest if he throws 150 innings in 2027.

The 29-year-old Martin threw 146 innings with a 3.95 ERA in 2026, but it was a 3.41 ERA in the first half and a 5.12 ERA in the second half. The White Sox kept him at arm's length in the postseason despite running bullpen games almost nightly. Martin allowed two runs in one inning in his only postseason appearance.

Neither Sullivan nor Veliz are significant prospects. For all intents and purposes, the White Sox are attaching Martin to Castillo as a sweetener to get the Rockies to take Castillo's salary. The Rockies are essentially buying Martin, who is under team control through 2030, by taking on the rest of Castillo's contract.

Here now are our trade grades for this two-for-two swap.

Fair or not, I'm going to lump the two Castillo trades together. Chicago stepped out to acquire Castillo at the deadline and absorbed the $30 million or so remaining on his contract to do it. Seranthony Domínguez, who had about $15 million left on his deal, went the other way in the trade, so the White Sox took on about $15 million total, and also gave up a pretty good prospect in Boston Smith.

Four and a half months later, the White Sox had to give up a steady back-end starter in Martin to clear Castillo's money. They ended up saving about $7 million in 2027 in this series of moves, but it cost them Martin and Smith (and Domínguez), and they had to endure 31 awful innings from Castillo. Unless Sullivan or Veliz hit big, the White Sox took a series of Ls here.

Credit to president of baseball operations Chris Getz for acknowledging a mistake with Castillo and acting quickly to unload him. It was costly, though. Martin isn't a star, but cheap back-end starters are very valuable. We'll see what Getz & Co. do with the savings. Presumably they'll invest in more pitching. Having to give up Martin to dump Castillo so soon is a stinker, though. Ouch.

The Rockies need all types of pitching (righty, lefty, starter, reliever, whatever) and it's not often they can convince quality (or even competent) free agents to come to Coors Field. They have to develop their own pitchers or trade for pitching, and in this instance, they took on Castillo's hefty salary to get Martin and his four years of control. Creative, if nothing else.

There is downside potential too. Martin has run below league-average strikeout rates and middling ground ball rates throughout his career. Pitchers who allow a lot of balls in play -- a lot of balls in play in the air -- are a poor match for Coors Field. It's good the Rockies spent and found a way to add controllable pitching. They just might not have picked the best pitcher.

After losing 104 games in 2026, there is no such thing as a bad dart throw for the Rockies. It's unlikely they would have been able to spend the $22.75 million on a free agent (at least not without overpaying), so taking on Castillo to get Martin is the next best thing. I like the thinking, even if I don't love Martin's profile in Coors Field.

#2530. Paul George embracing role as second option to Jayson Tatum: 'Not one of those guys that have to have an ego'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The entire basketball world has spent the past five months or so trying to figure out what exactly caused the beef, or, well, lamb chops and gravy, between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. The two coexisted harmoniously as teammates on the Boston Celtics for the better part of a decade. They won a championship together and reached the Eastern Conference Finals five times. That run ended this summer with Boston's stunning decision to swap Brown for Paul George and draft picks, and we've never quite gotten to the bottom of what's happened since.

We know the Celtics tried to trade Brown for Giannis Antetokounmpo. After moving Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, Brad Stevens spoke about the team's need to both spread its financial resources and its usage among a wider group of players. Celtics broadcaster Brian Scalabrine claimed that Brown went to the organization with a list of demands that, if not met, would be followed by a trade request. Brown's camp has denied this claim, and Scalabrine himself has walked it back. Marc Spears reported in July that he had heard Brown felt like the Celtics treated Tatum as though he was the organizational favorite.

Regardless, there are clearly some hard feelings here. Brown claimed last offseason that the 2025-26 season was his personal favorite as a professional. Tatum missed most of that season, and Brown had his best statistical season. Brown claimed early this season that Tatum has a "hell of a PR team," and then he snubbed him at tip-off before their first game as opponents, a Celtics victory. That game was owned by George, Brown's replacement in Boston.

So far, the partnership has been harmonious. George is outplaying Brown thus far this season. He's been among the NBA's very best 3-point shooters, has spearheaded a system shift in Boston's defense that has finally allowed the Celtics to generate some turnovers, and he's done so on fewer shot attempts per game (15.7) than Brown has taken in any season since the 2019-20 campaign. Boston's vision for the George fit has proven accurate, and that's been as true in the press as it has been on the court.

George addressed his partnership with Tatum in an interview with The Athletic on Wednesday, and he made it clear that his role is to "help JT," in clear deference to Boston's remaining superstar. "I'm just not one of those guys that have to have an ego," George said. "My ego comes from what I do on the court when the ball gets thrown up and how I impact the game and how I affect the game in all aspects. My ego doesn't have to come from me stroking it or me thinking I'm bigger than someone or better than someone.

"But with that is, I know where I'm at in my career. I'm at the end of my career. Tatum, JT has (many) more years ahead of him, and he's someone that I admired from afar. And to see where he's taken his game, how much better he's gotten and him having all the tools and weapons to be the best player in the league, how can I help that? How can I support that and get him there?"

George and Brown are fundamentally different players. Brown, younger and a better scorer off the dribble, was well-suited to lifting last year's Celtics to a surprising 56-win season despite their shorthanded roster. But George's superior shooting and low-maintenance playing style have suited Tatum perfectly, and the fact that he's at a point in his career in which he's eager to take a backseat to Tatum helps with whatever palace intrigue occurred between Tatum and Brown at the end of their joint run.

If Brown was indeed frustrated with the idea of playing second fiddle to Tatum, it hasn't shown in Philadelphia. His 76ers are 12-3, he's openly called them Tyrese Maxey's team, and he played a key role in recruiting LeBron James, another ball-dominant star, to join the team in free agency. His usage on this star-studded 76ers roster is at its lowest rate since the 2019-20 season. Clearly, this was not as simple as Brown wanting his own team as so many suggested.

But something created a rift in Boston that led to where we are now, and so far, everyone involved should be happy with how this has played out. The 76ers and Celtics have the two best records in the Eastern Conference. George is playing better in Boston than he ever did in Philadelphia. Tatum is playing better with George than he ever did with Brown. And Brown has become an essential component of a different contender rather than being forced to start from scratch on a bad team as he would have if he'd been traded to the Milwaukee Bucks for Antetokounmpo.

On the court, at least, egos haven't been a problem for anybody, and the deal is working out for everyone.
